statement: The unit of failure is one kernel transaction (batch), never the map; the pipeline has no whole-map restart path and no silent seed swap (MFCG City.hx catch-all and VG seed swap are the removed behaviours)
notes: evidence pointers: MFCG 24 restarts in 58 attempts (§5 intro); VG 4 of 27 attempts; profile-mfcg.md ST-8

statement: Each step's failure response is a short fixed ordered list: check, repair locally, retry that piece with its next stream, simpler shape, substitute (uncuttable block to court or green), omit and report; nothing on the list touches anything outside the failing piece
notes: plain-words restatement of the tier table

statement: Feasibility by construction before geometry (tier 0): S1 guarantees river descent, S2 derives stage budgets from demand, S3 sites the centre relative to the river and reserves castle, plaza and institution precincts, so hard constraints are met before fabric is cut
notes: principle is §5.1's; the stage guarantees are §4.2's

statement: Every stochastic step has a declared, bounded, deterministic ladder; every rung taken writes a report line with a cause code and its tier; the ladder path is replayable from the printed stream key
Invariants police validity, not regularity: FTG's sheared minority of quads and NG's wedge class are kept

Every limit that can change output is a work (operation-count) limit, never a time limit (GEO-2), and scales with the size of its scope (NF-S10); each stage declares its work limits (counts of kernel calls, proposals, candidates, skeleton events, recursion depth) as laws over its batch scope's counts, not fixed numbers per rung

WorkUnit = 'plots' / 'buildings' / 'households' / 'landHa' / 'frameCells' / 'latticeNodes' / 'faces' / 'vertices'; WorkLimitLaw { counter: string; unit: WorkUnit; perUnit: number; floor: number; log2?: boolean }; WorkLimits = WorkLimitLaw[] carried as StageDecl.workLimits
notes: StageDecl owned by §4.12/§14 (pipeline/scope); workLimits.json table owned by §7.6

statement: Work-limit law: limit = floor + perUnit x count(unit, scope); with log2 set (recursion depths) limit = floor + perUnit x ceil(log2(count))

count(unit, scope) reads only model values committed before the batch runs (request population via S2 demand and stage quotas, Allocation records, scope land area, frame cells, lattice size), never a measurement; a district batch gets a limit proportional to its district and a scoped re-run (edit, regeneration, replay) gets exactly the limit its scope had in the full run
Population bands restated: TOWN spans 1 500-10 000 inhabitants; METROPOLIS 30 000-120 000
A kernel call that reaches its count returns E_WORK_LIMIT (§3.1) and the ladder treats it like any other failure (F-WORK), so identical inputs take identical rungs on every machine

Work-limit coefficients are set by rule: each = 99.9th percentile of measured work per unit on B-CITY-lite x 1.5, computed by the spike or milestone that builds the stage and recomputed whenever the stage's code changes (a declared shift if output moves)

Work-limit confirmation (M1, then every nightly cost-model run, §13.2): the F-WORK hit rate per stage is flat across each population band - at the top of every band it exceeds the bottom's rate by at most 1 per 1 000 batches
restated_in: §5.2 F-WORK test 5137 ('hit rate flat across each rung's population band')

statement: Pre-decided fallback for a failing counter: raise its perUnit to the measured 99.9th percentile per unit at the band's top x 1.5 and re-run the sweep; a coefficient change that moves output is a declared shift (§6.4)

Wall-clock time is read only by @plat/api's worker host, never by a model package; it may postpone or resume a lazy tier (F-BUDGET-TIME) and write telemetry but never changes what is computed; a tier computed late hashes exactly like one computed at once
The millisecond budgets of §12 are reporting targets and cost tests only, never output-changing limits

Rationale: operation counts chosen over wall-clock watchdogs (a watchdog makes a throttled tab, slow laptop or busy CI give a different town); laws over population-derived counts chosen over fixed per-rung counts (fixed counts fire near band top, break §7.8's monotone population control, slack at bottom)
notes: judgment-call text; candidate to move out; restated as J-DET-3, J-DET-25 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Retries are not rerolls (LC-5): ladder retries (tier 3) draw from the 'attempt' key component, which restarts at 0 for every reroll of the scope entity with the same cap; New random advances the 'reroll' component (§6.1, §7.1), so every reroll has its full ladder
Content digest: the Merkle node of an entity's subtree computed with identity (address, lineage) and lifecycle left out - kinds, geometry and attributes only

New random is checked to change its scope (NF-D6): after re-derivation each scope entity's content digest is compared with its pre-event value; an unchanged entity advances its reroll once more and re-derives, up to reroll.maxAdvance times; if still unchanged it keeps its original reroll (nothing changes, not even lineage) and the report lists 'no alternative within the ladder'; advances run on the dry run's overlay so only the chosen result commits; the event stores the rerolls actually used so replay repeats neither comparison nor advances
reroll.maxAdvance is a table value, default 3

B-EDIT minimal scopes: New random on a block holding one plot, a plot with a one-building row site plan, a one-cell district, a ruined building, and a person whose every attribute path is locked either changes the scope's content or reports it - never a silent no-op, never an identity change without a content change

Requested features are counted by delivery tier: full (tier <= 3), degraded (tiers 4-5), omitted (tier 6); acceptance counts a tier-6 omission of a requested feature as a failure (§15.2); 'no restart path' is a design property, not an acceptance number

The seven tiers: 0 feasibility by construction; 1 constraint check (typed KernelResult / invariant, nothing committed); 2 local repair (attract, widen, merge, re-inset, re-claim, re-site); 3 bounded local regeneration (next ATTEMPT inside current REROLL); 4 simpler primitive (bent cut to straight cut on mean normal to perpendicular mid-run cut; skeleton to medial axis for labels / plain roof for roofs); 5 substitution (uncuttable block becomes court, green or landmark plot, NG's rule); 6 documented omission, never silent
Tier 3 cap: at most 3 attempts per reroll

Tiers 2-5 run inside the transaction on the overlay; tier 6 commits without the feature; no tier re-runs another stage and no tier rerolls anything outside the failing entity's scope, because every retry draws from (entity lineage, concern, reroll, attempt) and nothing else reads that stream (§6.1)
Rows marked with a dagger carry a ladder whose mechanism another area owns (named with its section); the row repeats that area's rungs so the table and §3-§4, §9 agree
notes: this is the explicit duplication the consistency pass removes

statement: F-NUM (precision failure of an optional chain; GEO-3): detection E_OUT_OF_RANGE, E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE, E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE, E_SELF_INTERSECT on optional chains, warnings W_SNAP_PASSES, W_ACUTE_CORNER; ladder for optional chains only (growth proposals, optional lanes, decorative lines): re-propose from the next attempt stream, then reject the chain with a report line (an uninsertable proposal is simply not a street)

Mandatory chains (coasts, shores, banks, rivers, wall traces, arterials, band and kerb edges, plot lines, user-drawn geometry) cannot fail for a precision reason after attraction; E_OUT_OF_RANGE on them is a bug that aborts the batch with its stream key; E_LOCKED goes to the dry run (F-EDIT)

B-FUZZ: 10^6 random concave, holed, thin, near-collinear, self-touching and snapped inputs per primitive plus constructive degeneracies (§13.1): 0 crashes, 0 hangs, 0 self-intersecting outputs, 0 undeclared slivers (O3 a); 0 mandatory chains rejected on B-CITY

F-CUT (bent cut fails; GEO-23) at S8, S10: detection E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS or a child failing simple/min area/min width/min angle; ladder: reflex pre-cut (face with a reflex vertex deeper than the band's block depth split from it first, and at antenna roots) -> redraw cut position x2 -> straight cut on the mean normal -> always-succeeding cut perpendicular to the longest side run through its midpoint, clipped to the face's own component -> substitution (court / green / landmark / joined plot for the largest unplaced class of the district's allocation, never live roster state, §4.7)
F-CUT substitution is allowed only for faces <= 2 x the band's upper block area

F-CUT property test: on 10^5 random concave and holed faces the ladder terminates in <= 6 kernel calls and the face count never decreases; built-area share left as court or green residue reported per district (soft band <= 5 %); NG signature regression (§13.5); MFCG baseline 19 skipped cuts and 3 of 16 cities restarted for 'bad poly'
values: 10^5 faces; <= 6 kernel calls; residue soft band <= 5 %; baseline 19 / 3 of 16

statement: F-CORRIDOR (union makes slivers or a collapsed block; GEO-35, GEO-4) at S9: a face below its class minimum width or area after corridorUnion; ladder: absorbSliver (merge across a partition edge, else keep face as 'residue'; a structural edge is never deleted) -> downgrade the offending lane to alley width -> retype the lane 'invisible' and log
B-CITY: 0 faces below their class minimum width and area; 0 structural edges deleted

F-OUTLINE (closed outline not simple; GEO-13) at S1 (coasts, lakes, islands, sky-island outlines): displaced outline self-intersects or loops; ladder: clamp the displacement -> repair by non-zero union -> type each resulting loop (islet / pond / absorbed), reported
Island, fjord and sky-island fixtures: 0 non-simple outlines committed

F-RIVER (no course / no crossing; GEO-36) at S1, S3 and S1's water operator: detection: descent stalls in a sink, carve depth would exceed carveMaxCm, course leaves the frame before the core, no crossing site in the core band; ladder: carve the sink deeper up to carveMaxCm -> re-trace from the last good knot -> move the inlet along the frame edge (attempt) -> move the centre to the bank (S3) -> declare 'no crossing', route arterials to the bank road, report; a requested river island whose branch separation fails is reported 'not built'

Inside an edit the F-RIVER re-trace is confined to the edited reach and the inlet and centre rungs are not offered (the edit is then declared Re-derive from S1, §7.3); a moved course knot (moveCourseKnot, §7.1) is never re-traced away from the user's position: a course through it whose carve would exceed carveMaxCm returns F-EDIT with the nearest position along the drag within the cap
restated_in: §5.2 F-EDIT detection 5139 (moved course knot beyond carveMaxCm)

statement: 1 000 seeds x {river, coast+river} x rung (WaterSetting spelling, §13.3; VS2-5, VS4-5): 'river within the core when requested' = 100 % (MFCG baseline: 7 of 10 attempts fail at size 80)

F-CONTOUR (contour crosses a shore; GEO-14) at S1; ladder: the coast construction of §4.2 S1, then clip every contour to the land faces in vector space before emission (always succeeds), reported; never an abort path
Steep-coast, cliff and spit fixtures: contours crossing water 0; 0 S1 aborts

F-SITE (no valid centre) at S3: every candidate fails slope/land/flood tests, or polycentric nuclei closer than the separation floor (§4.2 S3 (6)); ladder: relax the slope threshold one step -> the largest land component's centroid band -> report; for nuclei: re-site the later nucleus (<= 3) -> merge the two under one enceinte with a cross wall, reported
notes: no dagger: §5.2 is its home, though subject is S3

statement: F-SITE: corpus sweep over relief characters; twin-town fixtures: walls apart by the floor or one shared enceinte with a cross wall

F-ROUTE (no arterial path; GEO-17) at S4 and S4's local operator: detection E_NO_PATH, or an approach cannot meet a pinned bridge deck within the class's minimum radius; ladder: another crossing site on the reach within its search band (one S1 or S3 already emitted, a 'site' no way uses yet; river and canal decks; a moat deck is fixed at its gate; deck stays perpendicular to local flow) -> one bridge at extra cost (a new deck whose two deck_end vertices are placed by one L0 batch of two same-level shore splits, nothing cleared, before the way's L1 batch lays the span) -> relax the slope limit one class -> route to the nearest reachable junction and mark the destination 'unserved' in the report
notes: dagger row; open item NP5-2 (S5b main-road step not covered by any class)

statement: Inside S1's water operator (§7.3 (b)) or a carve (§4.11), whose new water is not yet inserted, F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung only sites the deck: its bank vertices are placed on the route by the operator's L1 batch and promoted by its L0 batch (§7.3 (b) 2-4; VD4-10)
Scripted requests on 100 seeds with pathological sites; O4 (a): 100 % of through-roads at a named destination or reported; road and deck agree on 100 % of crossings
notes: MFCG 'Unable to build a street!' logged but invisible (O16) - evidence

statement: F-BUDGET-STAGE (capacity below demand; FTG-2) at S5: detection S5d's area test (stage's grown area vs its plot demand at the bands' plot areas); ladder: one bounded top-up before the next stage (widen the stage boundary by the shortfall at the stage's measured plot density, grow only the added ring, recompute the trace) -> accept and report the shortfall; the exact plot check after S10 feeds F-SITING
B-CITY sweep over wealthLevel {0, 0.5, 1}: population within +/- 5 % on >= 95 % of seeds and the walled share in its band

F-WALL (bad trace / infeasible gate count; GEO-18, FTG-8, NF-P1) at S3, S5a, S7: detection: trace self-intersects or crosses the core; a closed trace does not close or an open trace end is not anchored on shore/bank/cliff; fewer arterial crossings than N; a non-gate way reaches the trace; ladder: two gate routes crossing the stage-1 boundary at one point -> re-draw the later gate pick (<= 3) -> drop it and report; trace fixed before growth with gates pinned: re-offset with a larger radius -> topology-preserving union-simplify -> anchor open ends by attraction onto nearest shore/bank/cliff (shared stretch carrying bank and wall) and add water gates where the waterfront policy requires a quay wall -> divert excess arterials to the nearest gate as lanes -> add posterns and report when N cannot be met (N = 0: declared sealed circuit, harbour gate still placed) -> last rung: cut a way reaching the wall at the setback band and prune the outer stub, reported

B-CITY: gates on arterials 100 %; main gates = N exact; roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates plus any §4.2 S3 (7) harbour gate (NP4-5); 0 non-gate crossings; 100 % of quays reachable without crossing a wall except at a gate on coastal and river seeds; MFCG baseline sealed cities at 0 main gates without fallback

F-CASTLE (compactness / overlap; MFP-3) at S3, S7: detection compactness < 0.75 or the claim overlaps water or the plaza; ladder at S3 (bailey sited, before the trace welds to it), inside the reservation: equalise the claim's angles (<= 20 passes) -> bloat in 5 % steps up to the band's top -> re-site (reported) -> keep without a bailey (reported)
Castle area and compactness in band on >= 99 % of B-CITY seeds; 0 ways through reservations; O8 (d); MFCG baseline 178 equalize passes and 11 bloats per census

F-PLOT (unusable plot; GEO-24) at S10: frontage < min, wedge angle < 12 deg, landlocked; ladder: per-frontage regions (when the block's skeleton downgrades, a reflex pre-cut partition instead) -> merge into the neighbour -> insert an alley to give access -> typed residue (court / vacant)
Invariants: every plot has >= 1 access edge (100 %); 0 landlocked buildings; NG baseline 42 % of lot leaves discarded

F-SITING (roster item unplaced; LC-2, FTG-1) at S10b: the eager allocation cannot place a class's demand in its affinity district; ladder: reconcile inside the district's allocation (JOIN at block granularity -> a whole block -> the district edge); cross-district moves only in the allocation's own reconcile (S7b) -> reduce the manifest and report 'unplaced'; decided eagerly, never by lazy-district placement order, never silently
O18 (f): 100 % of institutions on a plot meeting their requirement; districts derived in three random orders give identical digests (§6.5)

F-SITEPLAN (footprint does not fit; FTG-13) at S11 and the terrain operator: setbacks leave no rectangle >= the class minimum, or after a terrain stroke a row footprint's fall exceeds skirtMaxCm; ladder: on slopes above skirtMaxCm stepped wings first -> lower coverage one step -> next arrangement (compound -> detached -> hovel -> 'tents' row where the class allows) -> vacant plot typed yard, reported
O17 (f): 100 % of footprints fit; 0 renderer fallback rectangles

F-SKELETON (GEO-8, GEO-2) at S11, S13a: output validator fails (non-planar skeleton, non-monotone faces, inconsistent heights) or the skeleton's work limit (events processed) is reached (E_WORK_LIMIT, never a timeout); ladder: labels use a sampled medial axis (§3.8, used by §9.3); roofs a plain roof (VIS-11): footprint drawn with no ridge or hip lines, roof kind 'plain', heights unchanged; near-rectangular footprints never reach this row (exact OBB roof is the primary construction)
Ladder-coverage fixtures (§13.1) render every downgrade and assert no roof line outside its footprint; 0 crashes on 1 000 holed polygons

F-LABEL (no fit; GEO-29) at S13b view side: spine shorter than text at minimum size or unresolved collision at priority; §9.4's seven rungs: (1) preferred spine at size proportional to sqrt(area), never below the floor -> (2) short name form -> (3) straight label on the OBB axis, one line or two broken at a breakAt position -> (4) OBB arc -> (5) quarter tree (label yields to the smallest ancestor whose spine fits its own name at the floor; ancestor is one candidate per stop, §9.2) -> (6) declared overflow (<= 20 % of glyph area outside the face, never over a protected obstacle or another label) -> (7) legend entry (numbered disc + legend row, §9.5); floors in pixels; every rung counted in the report; placement is view data and never changes the model

'0 collisions' is a view invariant tested by B-ZOOM at settled views and during a zoom sweep; >= 99 % of all area-label glyph area inside its face, which caps the overflow rung at 5 % of on-map area labels

F-WORK (operation count reached) at any stage, ladder or kernel call: E_WORK_LIMIT when a declared count (candidates, proposals, kernel calls, skeleton events, recursion depth) is reached, each count the stage's law over its batch scope's population-derived counts (§5.1 (5)); ladder: the stage's declared coarser rung entered by the count, never by time (fewer candidates, larger cells, shallower recursion) -> report 'work_cut' with the count; map valid and identical on every machine

Golden suite under a time-dilation shim (every clock read x 10 and x 0.1): per-stage digests byte-identical; work-cut rate per stage reported on B-CITY; hit rate flat across each rung's population band (§13.2)

F-BUDGET-TIME (stage over its time budget; reporting and scheduling only, GEO-2) in the @plat/api worker host outside model packages: wall-clock watchdog; action: postpone or resume a lazy tier (cancel-and-resume only), telemetry records 'time_over', never a model change
A tier postponed and resumed hashes identically to the eager tier; per-stage timing against §12 in CI telemetry on reference hardware

F-EDIT (constraint conflict) at S0 and edits: detection: a drawn way crosses a locked entity; a targeted assignment names a locked entity; an assignment cannot be honoured within its drift bounds; a warp would break an invariant or carry a locked or pinned point-anchored record out of its host face (§7.4); the effective scope holds protected entities whose fate is not 'kept'; an undo or redo whose target has dependent live events (§7.4); a water edit's new channel + bank setback meets a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity, or a reservation (§7.3 (b) 3); a moved course knot beyond carveMaxCm (F-RIVER); a host provider's output that would pass the 2 MB cap on pack data and host content (§2.9)

F-EDIT resolution: the dry run returns the conflict as an action (nearest valid position, the blocking lock, the edit-fate list for confirmation, the dependent events to undo first, Re-derive from S3 for a reservation in a new channel's way, or the provider and size that passed the cap); precedence lock > assignment > drawn geometry > rules (§7.7); never silently resolved
B-EDIT sequences and conflict fixtures: 0 planarity violations, 0 lost faces, 0 silent re-binds
Host provider output cap: 2 MB on pack data and host content
notes: restated from §2.9; open item VD5-2 concerns the pack-copy cap conflict in §7.5

statement: F-REDERIVE (coarse re-derivation invalidates finer content or crossings; LC-7) in §7.3's local operators (S1 water and terrain, S4, S5, S6, S7): detection: a plot, footprint or yard in new water, in a new corridor, across a moved wall band or outside its new cell; a way that new water + its bank setback will meet off a deck (found on the new water's data before insertion, §7.3 (b) 1-2); a deck span no longer crossing water; a crossing 'site' whose bank vertices no longer stand on a shore of its reach

F-REDERIVE plots and buildings: re-cut the plot along the new boundary (ids kept by the anchor rule, §6.3) -> re-fit its site plan (F-SITEPLAN) -> demolish what still conflicts, with a lifecycle event whose cause is the edit

F-REDERIVE way meeting new water off a deck: applied before the water is inserted, in the L1 batch of S1's water operator (§7.3 (b) 3) and of a carve (§4.11 (1)), so the L0 insertion meets no finer edge except at the vertices that batch prepared (§3.3); an arterial, the only connection of streets beyond it to a gate or the plaza (§4.11's rule), or a way that crossed the changed water on a deck is re-routed through the nearest deck within the detour bound, a deck being sited for it by F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung when none does; every other way is cut at the bank setback (stretch inside new water + setback removed, each land part kept as a way: the part keeping the old anchor - end junction else larger overlap, §6.3 - keeps the address, the other is a fresh way) and a stub (land part shorter than the district's minimum block width ending at the setback) is removed, leaving a dead end at the bank
Detour bound for re-routing through a deck: re-routed length between the way's nearest pinned nodes on either side of the water <= 1.4 x the old length

A deck over land (reach moved away and §7.3's re-siting found no site in the band): the Bridge becomes a tombstone (demolish, cause the edit); its span stays in its way as an ordinary segment of the way's class (the higher class of the two joined ways where the span was a separate 'bridge' way) or leaves with the way if removed; its deck and deck_end rows are removed (removeEdges on ChainRef('deck', bridge) and on its two VertexRef('deck_end', bridge, i)); demotion then takes its bank vertices to the way's level and clears their kernel pins (§2.2 rule 3; VK4-1)
notes: kernel pin rule owned by §2.2 (model); open item VK5-2 touches the pin-release rule

statement: A site over land (reach moved away and no successor site matched it, §7.3 (b) 2): the site is removed - its deck_end rows by removeEdges on their VertexRefs, its record a tombstone (§2.7; §7.3 (b) 9; NP3-4, NP4-7)

Every re-cut, demolition, re-route, cut and pruned stub is listed in the edit-fate report with its lifecycle event; a locked or pinned entity is never demolished, re-routed or cut - its conflict returns to the dry run as F-EDIT

B-EDIT terrain-brush (both water modes), course-knot, drawn-water, drawn-way and drawn-wall sequences, including a river move across a street grid that commits with its decks and cuts and keeps every face outside its clear region byte-identical (§7.3 (b)): 0 hard invariant violations; 0 decks and 0 sites over land; 0 off-deck crossings (§5.3); 0 wings off §2.6's datum rule; 0 footprints in water; every demolition, cut and re-route has an event
Datum rule restated: a wing's baseCm = the highest terrain sample under the wing + the plinth, user-edited bases excepted

Every invariant declares a scope: batch-local (evaluated on the batch's touched faces plus their one-ring and on records the batch created, changed or removed), stage-end (once when a stage or its scoped re-run completes), save / load (when a document is written or verified), CI-only (test harnesses); only batch-local invariants run per batch

An edit's dry run (§7.1) evaluates the edit's batch-local and stage-end invariants once on the scratch overlay and the commit reuses that result (overlay committed as validated): one validation per edit, not two

For an edit whose operators chain several batches (§7.3 item 3), batch-local rows are evaluated once after the chain's last batch over the union of the chain's touched faces, their one-ring and the records the chain touched (a river move places deck bank vertices in an L1 batch before its L0 batch inserts water, so the crossing row holds only at chain end); the kernel's own invariants (§3.10, first row) still hold at every batch, so each chained batch keeps every way and enceinte one connected chain (§7.3 (b) 3)

Kernel invariants (batch-local; checked on the commit record's faces, edges, role keys): lattice points inside the range; no edge shorter than minEdge from any writer (insertion, booleans, buffers, offsets, smoothing, warp); clearance; simple faces except declared antennae; nesting by index (every level-(n+1) face has one level-n parent); the placement bound; level consistency; index freshness (every item a batch deletes, re-levels or changes tombstoned where its static copy lies; VK4-2, VK4-5); role consistency with no structural role lost
notes: restates §3.10; open item VK5-1 concerns the tombstone rule under district regroup

statement: Class floors: min width / area / angle per class, never minEdge as a face floor (GEO-35); batch-local on touched faces
No footprint overlap; batch-local, touched footprints against the spatial index
Every plot has >= 1 access edge and every building its entrance on one; batch-local on touched plots and buildings
No way centreline crosses a footprint; no way crosses a reservation (§4.2 S3); batch-local
notes: also §5.2 F-CASTLE test (0 ways through reservations)

statement: Walls not crossed by ways except at gates; batch-local on touched ways and wall edges

A way crosses water only on a deck and a deck only over water (LC-7): every way-role edge with both sides in water (L0 parents of both side faces are water) belongs to a Bridge's deck span (edges between its two deck vertices, carrying the deck role; fords included) or to a harbour work (VD2-2); every deck span crosses a water face with both ends on its banks; a wall trace crosses water only at a water gate; batch-local, checked by index against L0 parents of both sides (§2.2 rule 2)

Harbour work: a way of class pier or quay whose connected set of pier and quay edges meets land in at most one L0 land face (a pier, mole or breakwater arm rooted on one shore; a detached breakwater touching none, §4.8); it stands in water rather than crossing it; a pier or quay way joining two land faces across water must cross on a deck

Harbour-work check: for a touched pier/quay edge with water both sides, one walk of its connected pier and quay edges counting distinct L0 land faces its vertices touch (a harbour-wall row's few hundred edges at most); covers S1 river decks, S3 moat and canal decks, S5a outer-moat decks, carve decks and S7 harbour furniture; §13.2's harbour fixtures include a two-arm mole and a detached breakwater

NF-P5: no lane crosses a wall strip, and no L3 band, setback, glacis, tower or gatehouse face is cleared or split by an L1 or L2 batch - in every generation batch and every edit batch, except for enceintes whose wall-strip parts the edit's chain declares it rebuilds (S10 step (0)) or removes (VP2-4, VD3-6); a lane still never crosses a strip

NF-P5 exemption declaration: the dry run of every chained edit computes the set of enceintes whose strips any of its batches changes, each marked 'rebuilt' or 'removed'; every batch of the chain carries it; the check reads the declaration, never a list of edit kinds

Edits that declare an NF-P5 exemption today: tree-scoped re-derivation of a scope holding wall-strip faces (§7.3 item 2); S7's operator (drawWall, moved trace vertex, re-traced run, gateToJunction); S1's water operator for every wall strip its L1 batch changes (re-traced run's strips; a setback or glacis line it anchors and cuts outside a re-traced run, §7.3 (b) 3, 7, 8); a carve for every strip its batches (1)-(3) change and its step 4 re-derives (§4.11); removals: wallToWay, contractWall (§4.11) and an enceinte's delete (§7.1 walls row)
notes: list is informative; rule says the check never reads a list

statement: NF-P5 checks: touched lanes vs setback and wall edges; commit record's removed/changed L3 faces of kind band/setback/glacis/tower/gatehouse vs the declared enceintes; a CI registry test fails when an edit operator or conversion that can write a wall strip's L1 lines or L3 parts has no declaration path; §13.2 fixtures commit a canal carved across a wall between two towers and a river move whose new bank cuts a glacis line without crossing the wall with 0 NF-P5 violations; a drawWay lane across a strip is refused
Footprints intersect (wall band + setback) = empty on both faces of every wall (MFP-9); batch-local

Every building's wing rings (and a stored composition's composed wings) are simple, counter-clockwise and unite to its footprint face exactly (integer equality), after S11's first carry and after the carry following every later committed batch changing a footprint face (§2.6 wing-carrying rule; NP3-1, NP4-2, NP4-3); batch-local by §2.6 rule 4's tiered test (no union for a wing re-read whole, ring test with pairing for tiled wings, a union only for overlapping ones)
notes: cost figure is evidence; open items NP5-1 and NP5-4 touch compositions

statement: Water intersect footprints = empty; batch-local

Every built bridge lies within +/- 10 deg of the channel normal, measured on the deck and on the way (GEO-17); a 'site' has no span and is outside every deck row (§2.7; NP3-4); batch-local on touched crossings
Exclusive land uses never overlap; batch-local

Reference integrity: every reference out of a touched record (people and relations included; a dependent's carer resolves) names a live id; every reference into a record the batch removed is carried over (§6.3) or reported as an orphan; batch-local via the reverse-reference index
Identity: every fresh address differs from every live and tombstoned address, and no two live entities share a lineage key (§6.3); batch-local at mint, O(1) against the identity set
Every length field carries a unit; batch-local at schema write (and the lint of §2.1)

Label collisions are not a model invariant: placement is view data and '0 collisions' is tested by B-ZOOM (§5.2 F-LABEL, §9)

Telemetry { stageMs: Record<StageId, number>; timeOver: StageId[]; verifyMs?: number } - session-only, never saved, never in any digest

The generation report is a derived cache: rebuilt by every derivation and by the verification replay on load, saved only in the document's 'derived' section (so the panel shows it before verification finishes), excluded from the canonical form and every digest (LC-24)
The report records stream keys only for ladder uses (any rung from tier 2 up, retries at attempt > 0 included), not for every stream the town used (SCL-11)
Timings are telemetry: measured by the worker host outside model packages, shown by the UI; nothing saved or hashed contains a millisecond
The same report object is the UI's compact dismissable panel (O16) and the API's report(doc); every ladder use is replayable from its printed key (MFCG's replayable attempts kept)

Plain-words promise: the same seed makes the same town on any computer; decisions counted in steps never seconds; non-integer maths via a bit-identical library; the digest is kept up to date incrementally; every part draws from its own stream named by where it came from, so adding a decoration kind or naming rule, re-rolling one block or growing a stage never reshuffles what exists; not promised: a release that changes an early step changes towns built on it and says so stage by stage; edited towns keep their edits through permanent addresses separate from random streams
RNG engine: xoshiro128** per stream (four 32-bit words; period 2^128 - 1; fast in JS, no BigInt)
Keys are mixed from structured components, never from strings (SCL-12, K-6 / R-1 kept); no string is built on the generation path
Seed key (128 bits) is derived once from the seed by four 32-bit-lane finalisers with distinct salts, all Math.imul
Entity key = mix of seed key, lineage hash, layer and island (§6.3), computed once at mint and cached in the arena beside the lineage hash

Town-level draws (S0 feature draws, terrain noise, per-document furniture: compass and emblem, §9.5) use the town root's entity key = seed key mixed with the fixed town lineage (ground arena, no parent, creation epoch 0, index 0), so they depend on the recipe alone, never on docId
Paint programs and furniture pass the reserved stage id STAGE_VIEW = 0xffff to the one mixer (§14 Rng.stream; NF-D12)

Stream key = one finaliser round over the entity key combined with packed components (stage id u16, concern id u16, reroll u16, attempt u8, epoch u16, salt u16); its four words seed the state directly; the all-zero state is replaced by a fixed nudge
A stream is created once per derivation and continued; a second request in the same derivation returns the same stream
Textual stream-key form for reports only, rendered from the same components: S11/siteplan@plot:7kq2m9x4c1b0a/arrangement[/r=1][/a=2][/e=0]

Stream-key derivation budget <= 0.1 us per key (string paths measured 0.73 us, SCL-12); measured by the M0 (d) determinism spike over a B-CITY city; pre-decided fallback: derive a batch's keys in one vectorised pass over a typed array (output-neutral, no golden moves)
Lineage component: the entity's stream identity - layer, island, derivation unit, stage, creation epoch, creation index; kept by a surviving entity so nothing that survives is re-rolled
Concern component: what the draw is for (registry); streams are never shared across concerns

Reroll component (LC-5): the scope entity's New random count, an absolute number stored in its identity and written into the regenerate event as an explicit per-entity map (rerolls actually used, §5.1 (6)); children draw with their derivation unit's reroll, so New random on a block changes that block's plots and nothing else
A user's reroll count is capped at 32 767; rerolls 32 768 and above are reserved for §13.2's faithfulness references (§7.3 item 7 (iv))

Attempt component: the ladder's retry number (§5.1), restarting at 0 inside each reroll; its cap is declared per concern in the registry: 3 for every geometric ladder (tier 3), 8 for the naming re-draw of §9.6 (a repeated name re-draws on its own stream before taking a distinguishing suffix)
Epoch component: e for draws made by epoch e; epoch 0 is the original town

Salt component (COV-VG-VN-008): a per-concern number in the recipe (default 0) that rerollLayer(concern) bumps (§7.1), only for rerollable concerns: naming, render.instances, style.jitter, style.crowns, style.compass, naming.emblem (read by the compass furniture program and the emblem generator, §9.5); geometry concerns take no salt (their reroll is the regenerate action), so rerolling trees or names moves nothing else
The recipe's initial salts are keyed by the same registry-generated type and its schema refuses any other key (§2.9; VD3-8), so no recipe, link delta or log can give a geometry stream a salt

A town-wide rerollLayer sets the concern's town salt; an ids-scoped rerollLayer of naming (VD2-10) re-draws only the names of the listed entities, each with the per-entity salt the event carries in place of the town salt

Every other draw of a name uses the town salt (entity with no predecessor) or, when the name's naming inputs changed, the salt its last draw used, held in the name's naming record (§6.3 cases (1) and (4), §2.8; VD3-2); a name's salt is never in the model digest: the setting event holds it and the naming record caches it

The registry marks a concern rerollable only when a StageDecl.streamKeys entry or a paint program names it; rerollLayer's concern type is generated from those entries; a CI test fails when a rerollable concern has no reader (N-18)

Label candidates are geometric (S13a, §9.3) and placement is a deterministic greedy over a total order (S13b, §9.2), so no labels stream is registered; 'reroll the labels' is not offered; re-placing a label is moveLabel
Ordinal-keyed draws (roster's prefix-stable roster/<class>/<ordinal>, §10.2, FTG-14) use the class's registry entry as derivation unit and the ordinal as creation index through the same mixer

Concern registry (G-P6): adding a concern is a reviewed change to a registry file; concern ids are u16, append-only, never renumbered, so adding one changes no other key; each entry declares its reader stages, whether it is rerollable and its attempt cap

Initial concerns (63 names): terrain.noise, terrain.controls, water.coast, water.river, water.islands, water.delta, site.centre, blueprint.features (S0 per-rung feature draws §4.2), intent.surprise (§7.7), gate.pick, reserve.plaza, reserve.castle, reserve.precinct, reserve.water, roster, route, growth.heading, growth.branch, growth.mainroad, growth.curvature, district.seed, district.type, alloc.district, alloc.block, field.chance, cut.t, cut.side, cut.arc, cut.width, cut.farSideAlt, plot.width, plot.join, plot.vacancy, plot.bounds, siting, siteplan, siteplan.template, heights, material, greenery, fields, crop, forest, hinterland.outside, hinterland.decor, pin.centrepiece, pin.decor, pin.stall, people, content/relations, naming, naming.quarter, naming.emblem, warp.jitter, epoch.transform, island.place, sewer, style.jitter, style.crowns, style.compass, render.instances, style.random, render.stampTiles

render.stampTiles concern (§8.10; NR4-1, NR-6, NR3-7): non-rerollable, attempt cap 0; stream keyed by a constant entity key over (stamp-tile domain, decoration class index, reference spacing 400 cm, creation index 0-3 for the class's four tiles, 4 for their shared border band) with STAGE_VIEW; read by @plat/kernel's poisson builder when plat/tools/stamptiles/ builds the shipped asset, and in a worker only by the fallback rebuild of a tile whose hash differs; appended so no other key moves
Registry notes: alloc.district also draws S7b's edge-green-or-orchard choice per district, and island.place the sky allocations' areas (§4.5 S7b (4)-(5)); no concerns of their own

Distinctness (LC-29): a CI test asserts every stream key and lineage hash in a B-CITY city and in a sky-island fixture (two islands carrying districts, underground tunnels) is distinct; birthday bound negligible (2^128 for stream keys; approx 3 x 10^-10 per city of 10^5 entities for 64-bit lineage hashes, and §6.3's collision rule covers even that); the test guards the encoder, not the arithmetic

Draw helpers: u32; float01 = (u32 >>> 8) x 2^-24; int(lo, hi); bool(p); normal() = Irwin-Hall of 12 uniforms (no transcendental in the RNG layer, G-R12); fuzzy(f); weighted(table); deck(table) (draw without replacement, MFCG DeckRuleSelector idea); NG roof jitter's 6-uniform pseudo-normal is a style-time helper

Decoration (LC-20, VIS-5, SCL-8): trees, scatter, crowns, roof detail and hatch phase are keyed by the entity's render key (low 64 bits of its entity key, mixing seed key and lineage, §8.1 item 5; VD2-6) and the instance ordinal, never by LOD band

Nothing about decoration is stored except the user's instance overrides (instance events, §7.1) and the current positions of positional overrides in the entity's override table, which a warp or vertex move carries with the ground (§7.4; VK2-13)

Enter (LC-28, COV-VG-WC1) creates a new document with seed (seed + 1) mod 2^32 (Seed is a u32, §2.9) and the same recipe - params, intent, character, entry mode, table pins, packs - without edits, locks, assignments or salts; when the current document has edits the app first warns and offers to save it

statement: The Recipe (§2.9) holds every model-affecting input that is not an event: seed, rung, table pins, setting packs by id, version and content hash (selected user corpus included), full effective parameter delta with preferences folded in, intent, character, circumstance schedule, entry mode, rerollable concerns' salts

Host-supplied tables, presets and styles are not in the recipe: they arrive as logged editTable, editPreset and setStyle events whose content is copied into the log (§6.5 (8), §7.6); packs a later adjust adds are named by that event and belong to the document's pack set (§2.9)

Nothing else reaches the model (VD2-7): no wall clock (every output-affecting limit is an operation count, §5.1); no host text engine (label placement S13b is view data per zoom stop from names, LabelEntity records and bundled fonts' metrics, not in the digest); no viewing order (lazy only under §4.1's laziness contract, tested by random district permutations §6.5); no worker timing (results merge in lineage order); one boolean and offset engine per output version on every host (§6.5, D-14); no host code (host provider outputs read from hostContent on replay, §6.5, §2.9); no installed pack (packs resolved by content hash from the document's packs block then shipped packs; missing or mismatched opens read-only, §2.9); no machine preference read at run time (user-global preferences folded into the recipe at document creation, §7.6)
Laziness contract restated: a stage may be lazy only if its output for district D is a pure function of eager upstream state and D's own streams, reading no other district's lazy output

Pack resolution restated: every pack of the pack set resolved by content hash, from the document's packs block first then shipped packs; a missing pack or hash mismatch opens the document read-only (§2.9)
Two machines or browsers produce identical model digests (O2 a); two renders of one model are pixel-identical at a given backend, DPR and style version
notes: pixel identity subject may be rendering §8

statement: The model digest is a Merkle digest over the eager model's content only (SCL-1, LC-25, LC-2); the eager model = everything the city LOD draws plus town-level Allocation and FieldBands records (§4.5, §4.7); lazily derived content (close-ups, people, stage-3 compositions) enters when an edit materialises it
CI derived-complete digest: derive everything - every district, in three random orders, workers on and off, on 50 METROPOLIS seeds - and require identical results (§6.5)

Merkle formulas: leaf(record) = H128(kind, id, lineage, parent, existence, flags, attributes in schema order, digests of owned faces and chains); node(n) = H128(tag(n), children digests sorted by address id); root = node(model) per layer

Digest layers: site (terrain raster, fields, L0 water); network (ways, junctions, walls, gates, towers); districts (district, block, plot, buildings, yards, households, pins); hinterland; content (Allocation, FieldBands, institutions, factions, relations); names and LabelEntity records; closeups (edited close-ups only); identity (tombstone ids and supersededBy links, the lifecycle event block); plats (per arena and per level, the kernel's level digests)

Geometry is hashed once by the kernel per level (GEO-1): each arena keeps a digest per level over its level-n route (vertices, roles, face owners and kinds of level <= n, never arena slots), updated along each commit record's dirty set (§3.3); a finer level's Steiner vertices belong to the finer digest, so deriving L3 never changes the L2 digest
notes: per-level digest mechanism likely also in §3.3

statement: Per-level digests read each vertex's and edge's current birth level: a promotion (§2.2 rule 3) moves a vertex into the coarser digest from that commit on; a demotion moves it back out (the neighbour step's reversal restores the kerb's L2 digest exactly); kept finer content (§3.3) keeps its digest leaves through a coarser re-derivation (VK-18, VK-1)
An entity's leaf takes the digests of the faces and chains it owns (FaceRef, ChainRef resolved), so no coordinate is hashed twice

Digest input canonical order: a level-n ring starts from its lowest-then-leftmost vertex of level <= n, finer vertices skipped (§3.3's key; VK2-4); integers as 32-bit lanes, doubles as IEEE-754 bit patterns (-0 normalised to +0; NaN refused by schema), strings as UTF-8; no text serialisation on the digest path; no byte-order dependence

H128 = MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit variant (published public-domain algorithm in 32-bit ops; own implementation tested against published test vectors), seed 0, so the digest hash is specified exactly as H32 is (§13.6 (2); VS2-6)

Digest inclusion: names and LabelEntity records (text, candidates, pinned, hidden) are model data and hashed; excluded: provenance, derivation records and naming records (provenance digest §2.8; records digest below); style, view, derived, hostContent and telemetry (§2.9); label placement decisions (S13b view data); never-edited close-ups (a close-up is a pure function of its district's committed state, sub-seed, strategy and params, and enters under closeups with its first edit; LC-18, §7.4)
Digest maintenance: at every batch commit the kernel re-hashes the leaves of touched records and the nodes on their paths to the root, O(touched x depth), never by serialising the model (§3.3)

The maintained tree is built by the generation run in a session and, for a loaded document, by the load's one full recomputation from the decoded snapshot under the model packages of the document's own output version (§2.9 step 3; VD3-1, VD4-1); the snapshot stores only the root; every edit from the first after opening maintains a complete tree
Digest tree memory at CITY approx 1 MB (approx 30 000 entity leaves, approx 15 000 face-ring hashes and interior nodes at 16 B each), inside §12.8's entity-store line
Canonical text serialisation (sorted keys, integer coordinates, floats as shortest round-trip strings) is used only for golden files and exports

Records digest (VD4-6): persisted derivation and naming records (§2.8) form a second Merkle tree: one leaf per record = H128(id, record kind, fields in schema order, each cited slice as (table, version, kind, key, hash)); one node per static-index partition over its records sorted by address id (the partition whose entity chunk holds the record, §2.9); a root over the partition nodes
notes: open item VD5-4 (records with no district partition; re-hash scope)

statement: Records tree memory approx 0.25 MB of leaves and nodes at CITY, inside §12.8's entity-store line with the model tree

The records-digest leaf encoding belongs to the file schema, not an output version (records are stored inputs, not derived output): any version checks it, and a schema transform that changes a record column (§7.5) checks the old root and writes the new one

Records digest maintenance: exactly as the model tree - a batch that rewrites a record re-hashes its leaf and partition node; finalised when read; stored in the snapshot as recordsDigest; recomputed by every load with the model tree

Records digest recompute measured approx 4 ms at CITY and approx 11 ms at METROPOLIS for approx 10 900 derivation and 3 500 naming records at CITY (approx 29 300 and 9 500 at METROPOLIS), synthetic workload on reference machine, two runs within 0.1 ms (docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r5_recordsdigest.out); PLAUSIBLE until M0 (d) times it in the engine under the same 150 ms bar
The records digest is not a model digest: goldens, the locality oracle and the bridge's convergence read the model digest alone

Rationale: separate records digest chosen over folding records into the model digest (a re-encode-only release would become a declared output shift) and over leaving records unchecked (a wrong stored record silently changes later faithful regeneration or corpus selection)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-49 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Digest bars (M0 d, decided before any golden is signed): maintenance <= 5 % of each batch's own time at CITY; root finalisation at a stage end <= 5 ms at CITY; full recomputation of the root from leaves <= 150 ms at CITY, records tree included - used by the CI oracle and by every load (§2.9 step 3)

Full recompute measured approx 31-34 ms at CITY and approx 95-101 ms at METROPOLIS for the model tree (records tree approx 4 and 11 ms more), synthetic workload (docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r4_loaddigest.out; VD3-1); PLAUSIBLE until M0 (d)
No digest fallback moves a golden, because the root is a pure function of the leaves whenever it is computed (VD2-9)
Fallback (i) maintenance over 5 %: leaves re-hashed at the next coarser batch boundary (per district instead of per block and plot); the root at every stage end unchanged

Fallback (ii) root finalisation over 5 ms: layer nodes stay maintained at every commit; the root over them is finalised only when read - at save, end of a verification replay, export, API digest request, each stage end of a CI golden run

Fallback (iii) full recomputation over 150 ms: the CI oracle recomputes per run one subtree per layer chosen by the run's seed (every subtree covered across nightly runs) and compares with the maintained node

Fallback (iii) load path: the load takes a copy-on-write checkpoint of the decoded state at h0 (§7.4 checkpoints, chunked per district), makes the working state editable at once, recomputes model and records trees from the checkpoint in the generation worker between edits; edits made meanwhile keep their touched sets (§7.4) and are re-hashed on the new trees in log order at the end; roots at h0 compared with model.digest and model.recordsDigest as in step 3; a mismatch is a corrupt cache: the replay's state replaces the working state at the head and edits made meanwhile are re-applied in log order as 'take the replayed town' does (§2.9 step 4), fates recomputed and differences reported; nothing reported verified before the roots match

Until the roots match (VD4-2): 'trust the saved town' and step 4's keep are shown disabled; a save, an export, an API digest request and a bridged client's comparison of its root with a rebase's stateDigest wait for the recomputation and complete when it does; edits do not wait; a mismatch withdraws the keep for good (a corrupt cache is never a base)

Rationale: gate keep, saves and digest reads on the off-path recomputation rather than holding edits; off-edit-path checkpoint recompute chosen over per-chunk digest nodes in the snapshot (digest tree organised by layer and containment, chunks by partition; per-chunk nodes would need restructuring and §2.9's chunking fallback would change them)
