statement: A New random made during the off-path recomputation computes its scope's content digests from the scope's own leaves (§5.1 (6)), needing no tree

Two identities per entity (LC-1): an address that everything points at (edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports, the host) and a lineage that keys its random streams; they start equal and separate only when an entity is re-derived

Lineage key = (arena key - layer and part, §2.2 -, derivation unit's lineage hash, stage, creation epoch, creation index, derivation unit's reroll[, dup]); lineageHash = its 64-bit hash, cached in the arena
restated_in: §6.1 lineage component 5264 (lists layer, island, derivation unit, stage, creation epoch, creation index - no reroll or dup)

statement: Derivation unit (declared per stage in the registry): town for S4 routes (destination order) and S6 districts (seed order); growth stage for S5 ways (acceptance order); the L1 cell a way split, for new cells (split ordinal); the cell for S8 blocks and lanes; the block for S10 plots and alleys; the plot for S11 buildings, yard parts and households; the household for people (member ordinal); S6's run for Seam records (creation index by the run's lowest-then-leftmost vertex); the S5c growth run, the district's S8 run (baseLane portals) or the creating edit for portals; the creating edit event (its seq) for anything a user draws or builds; for any other kind (cells and junctions made by a growth commit, walls, water bodies, bridges, greenery) the stage run that created it
Creation index = the deterministic creation order of the unit's run, or the canonical order the stage declares (faces and vertices: by lowest-then-leftmost lattice point)

Address id = kind:token, prefixed <layer><island>/ outside the ground layer (sky2/plot:..., under/tunnel:...; LC-29); generated token = base-32 of the lineage hash at creation (13 characters); user-created token = hash of the creating event's seq and its ordinal; opaque - parent is a field, never parsed from the id
Rationale: lineage-hash tokens chosen over a per-kind high-water counter because a counter depends on lazy-district and worker mint order
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-1 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Never reused; one collision rule: minting runs after succession matching; a fresh entity whose natural address equals a live address, a tombstone or an address its own batch retires takes suffix ~k with the smallest free k; a fresh lineage key equal to a live entity's outside the batch's re-derived set (a survivor) takes the smallest free dup component; entities the batch itself replaces are not collisions (lets faithful Regenerate re-mint and reproduce them); collisions resolved in the batch's canonical order (records sorted by lineage hash)

An address that an undo withdraws (§7.4) is free again, but only the same derivation (same unit, lineage and reroll - what a redo or repeated New random re-runs) can mint it, so nothing is re-bound to an unrelated entity
Carry-over applies whenever a scope is re-derived: regenerate, Adjust, re-derive from Sk, a §7.3 local operator, template replacement, migration, epoch

Survival: an entity not re-derived (outside the invalidation set, a fixed input - locked, pinned, edited or assigned, §7.2 - or merely re-parented) keeps its address and lineage (its draws do not change); only its parent field and a reparent lifecycle event change

Succession: a re-derived entity is matched by anchor; the fresh entity of the same kind and class family whose anchor lies nearest within the kind's hysteresis radius succeeds it - takes the old address and old generated name with its naming record (references re-bind; §7.3 decides which overrides move) and keeps its own fresh lineage (New random really re-rolls); a carry event records the lineage change; the same batch re-owns the successor's faces and roles under the address (setOwner, retypeEdges, §3.4)

An old entity with no successor becomes a tombstone in the archive (§2.8) whose supersededBy names the fresh entity covering its anchor point, if any; a fresh entity with no predecessor keeps its fresh address

Lifecycle events are written only for changes (existence, flags, a lineage change, supersession, re-parenting), so a re-derivation that reproduces its entities exactly leaves the model digest unchanged
Rationale: only the address passes to a successor and lineage is kept only for survivors, because New random must re-roll its scope while references must follow the building the user means
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-2 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Names follow the address (VD2-10, VD3-2): a generated name (text and short form) is handed to a successor with the address together with its naming record (§2.8: naming slices its last draw consulted and the salt used), as a lock or assignment is; a re-sited bridge, a re-cut street and a regrouped district keep their names

S13a draws a name only in four cases: (1) entity with no predecessor, town salt; (2) every unedited name under a town-wide rerollLayer(naming), new town salt; (3) entities an ids-scoped rerollLayer lists (§7.1), each with its per-entity salt; (4) an unedited generated name whose naming inputs changed, with the salt its record holds

Case (4) triggers whenever S13a runs over the name's entity: after an adjust of the pack list (pack added/removed, corpus selected/deselected, §7.6); after an editTable or editPreset changing a naming slice (§7.6 invalidation by slice); in an upgrade's mapping (§7.5); at the event ending the name's protection (unlock or unassign that frees it; undo, redo or revert removing the setAttr, lock or assign that held it; §2.8 dormant record; VD4-3); in any re-derivation whose scope reaches S13a; it compares every slice the record cites with the current effective tables, and a slice whose hash differs or no longer resolves re-draws the name
notes: open item VD5-3 (frozenImport rebase and naming records), VD5-1

statement: Each field of a culture or ancestry row is its own naming slice - the (row, field) pair, hashed over the field's value and, for a corpus field, the named corpus's content hash (§7.6; VD4-5); a name's record cites only the fields its draw read, so selecting another corpus for one field re-draws exactly the names drawn from it (a street list renames that culture's streets, never districts or quarters)
A carried name is kept exactly while its naming inputs are unchanged; a change of features a grammar guard reads (a district that lost its gate) is not a naming input and renames nothing (§9.6)
Every name draw uses the entity's naming stream (keyed from its entity key, §6.1, with its case's salt and the attempt) and writes the name's naming record anew

Case (3) salts: the dry run gives each listed entity the salt one above the largest its name has been drawn with (town salt and every earlier ids-scoped salt); a re-drawn name equal to the old one advances the salt once more, up to reroll.maxAdvance times (as §5.1 (6)); the event stores the salts actually used so replay repeats neither

Case (4) renames: the dry run lists every rename (old and new text) in the edit's fate report with its other unprotected consequences; the edit commits after the user confirms; confirmed renames are stored in the event (EditBase.renames, §7.1; VD4-4); a replay or receiving client re-draws them identically, and one that computes different renames reports a mismatch as for fates (§7.3 item 4)
notes: open item VD5-1 (upgrade re-reporting of stored renames)

statement: A user-set name (setAttr) is an edited attribute, a locked name path a fixed input and an assigned name held at its assignment (§7.7); none is re-drawn while protected, and each keeps its naming record dormant for the event that ends the protection (§2.8; VD4-3)

When carrying or a re-draw brings two equal names into one uniqueness scope (§9.6; a district merge joining two same-named lanes), the entity whose address sorts later re-draws on its own stream, and the rename is listed in the edit's fate report

Rationale: generated name handed on with the address (a name belongs to the thing the user means); re-draw exactly the unedited names whose recorded slices changed (a list or rule edit must change what it produced and nothing else)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-37, J-DET-41 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Anchors and hysteresis (GEO-34): matching by distance, never quantised cell; candidate (old, fresh) pairs within the radius and of the same class family sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned one-to-one greedily in that order

Plot anchor: highest-class frontage (way address, start offset along the way); radius 0.5 m along the same way or its successor; class family = use family (residential, commercial, institutional, agricultural)
Building anchor: footprint centroid; radius 0.5 m; class family = building class family (a table row: small dwellings; halls and manors; religious; workshops and stores; towers and keeps; ...)
Block and cell anchor: centroid; radius 2 m (block), 5 m (cell); no class family
District anchor: its seed feature's address (same feature); class family district kind family
Way anchor: its end junctions' addresses, else overlap >= 50 % of its length; class family way class family
Junction, gate, tower, pin anchor: position; radius 1 m (junction, pin), 2 m (gate, tower); family = kind

Bridge anchor (LC-7): its deck's midpoint on the same river (water body address or successor); radius = the crossing-site search band of §4.2 S1 (5) (crossing.searchBandM, default 120 m); family kind (bridge, ford)
notes: searchBandM value owned by §4.2 S1 (5) / §7.6 tables

statement: Enceinte, water body, greenery, land use anchor: overlap >= 50 % (IoU); family kind
Household anchor (plot address, ordinal); person (household address, ordinal); label: target address
Seam (NF-P6) anchor: its two districts' addresses and its first chain's address (same pair and chain)
Portal anchor: position, radius 1 m, family portal kind (baseLane, growth, edit)
Split through an anchor: when a cut passes exactly through an anchor point, the child left of the directed cut keeps the id (the kernel returns children in that order, §3.6 (5))

Households and people (LC-16): a household's address survives a re-derivation of its plot by succession (anchor plot address and ordinal), so a person's key (household address, member ordinal, birth epoch; §10.3) is stable wherever the household is

Bridges: when S1's water operator re-sites the crossings of an edited reach (§7.3), each old deck is succeeded by the re-sited deck nearest its old midpoint within the band, so the bridge keeps its name, assignment and its way's reference

Anchor stability measurement (M1, B-EDIT-lite): 1 cm perturbations of every vertex keep >= 99.9 % of addresses; pre-decided fallback: building and plot radii double to 1 m and an IoU >= 0.5 test joins the class-family check

Matching routine (NF-D7): one routine hands addresses on in every re-derivation (scoped regeneration, Adjust, Re-derive from Sk - from S1 the whole town -, a local operator, template replacement, epochs, migration, §7.5 upgrade mapping); point-anchored kinds (plots by frontage offset, buildings, blocks, cells, junctions, gates, towers, pins, bridges) via a uniform grid per (kind, class family) with cell = the kind's hysteresis radius so every candidate is in the 3 x 3 neighbourhood, pairs sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned greedily; overlap-anchored kinds (ways without matched end junctions, enceintes, water bodies, greenery, land use) take candidates from the kernel's spatial index (§3.3) and compute overlap on those only
Matching budget: <= 2 us per re-derived point-anchored entity and <= 20 us per overlap-anchored one, median, included in §12.6's scope costs

Matching measured (Apple M1, Node 24; docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r2_match.out) on synthetic anchor sets: 0.60 us/entity for a 450-building district regeneration; 0.59 us for a 30 000-entity CITY re-derivation (0.38 us when unrelated); 0.59 us for an 80 000-entity METROPOLIS mapping at 2 m radius; to be measured in-engine at M0 d then M1 on B-EDIT-lite and a Re-derive-from-S1 fixture

Matching pre-decided fallback: match per static-index partition (§3.3) - candidates first from the entity's own district partition, only unmatched ones across partitions; a declared shift (§6.4) because a boundary entity can take a farther in-district candidate

JOIN and SPLIT: a joined plot takes its address by the anchor rule from the member whose frontage anchor it keeps; other members become tombstones with supersededBy = the joined plot; members is history; a later SPLIT resurrects a member whose anchor matches (the one permitted reuse of a tombstoned id, recorded as a resurrect event; safe because JOIN member ids were never given to another entity)

Document identity (LC-28): docId (UUID) minted at document creation, kept on save, re-minted on clone and save-as; addresses are document-scoped (a clone keeps them); at the API and bridge boundary every id is rendered <docId>/<id>; exports carry addresses and a supersedes table (tombstone to successor)
Workers merge results in lineage order, never arrival order
restated_in: §6.2 5361 (no worker timing - merge in lineage order)

statement: Scope of stability (O2 b, e; LC-3): (1) independent concerns - adding or changing a concern changes no other concern's draws; a naming-input change re-draws only names whose records cite it; (2) scoped rerolls - New random changes nothing outside its effective scope (§7.3); (3) upstream changes - a change to stage k's code or tables changes stage k's outputs and what derives from them, a declared cascade shift (§6.4, §13.3), never silent; stages upstream of k and independent of it stay byte-identical; (4) edited documents - stability across such changes comes from carry-over by anchor and migration (§7.5), never from stream keys

Identity measurement (M0 d and M1): minting and matching within budget; B-EDIT fixtures: drawBoundary, district merge and split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, a course-knot move re-siting a bridge (keeps address and name), New random on a district (matched successors keep names; only entities without predecessor draw), a district merge joining two equal lane names (later address re-draws, reported), the recycling case (a superseded assigned building whose creation slot is reused)

Naming-input fixtures (VD3-2, VD4-5, VD4-3): selecting a user street-name corpus renames exactly the unedited names citing the replaced (row, field) slice, listed in the fate report and stored in the event, all other names and naming records byte-identical, and a later re-sited bridge keeps its new name; a culture row naming a street corpus and a district-name corpus with its street corpus replaced keeps every district and quarter name byte-identical; setAttr-rename then undo, and lock then unlock, each around a corpus selection, re-draw by case (4), listed and confirmed, and the kept and truncated log give one digest; an editTable of one naming grammar row renames exactly the unedited names citing it; all hold in a rebased document (no provenance) as in a fresh one: 0 duplicate ids, 0 silent re-binds

Output version (o<k>): the observable output of the model packages; bumps exactly when a release declares a shift (any stage digest moves on the golden suite, §13.3); a release changing no output keeps it, so documents, links and goldens stay valid; every document and link names the output version it replays under
Generator version: the code build; informational (bug reports), never a replay key
Schema version: the file format (§7.5)

Preview flag (LC-19): links and documents made before output version 1 (fixed at M4's exit, §16) carry preview: true (in a link &pv=1) and the app shows §13.3's preview notice; the flag disappears from output version 1 on
Table versions: each rule table separately, pinned in the recipe; a table change that changes output is part of an output-version bump; a user override carries its base row's hash (§7.6)

Pack versions: each setting pack by id, version and content hash in the recipe or in the adjust event that adds it (§2.9 pack set); shipped packs belong to the output version like its tables (each retained version's chunk carries its own); a non-shipped pack's content travels in the document (NF-D2); a pack a later version stops shipping is copied into the document by the upgrade to that version (§7.5; VD4-9); a selected user corpus is a non-shipped pack user:<content hash> (§2.9; VD2-8)
notes: open item VD5-2 (pack copy past the 2 MB cap), VD5-6

statement: Style version: style sheets; changes pixels, never the model digest; carried in a link for pixel identity

Permalinks (LC-15, NF-D2) carry the canonical recipe, never a pointer to machine state: ?o=<output version>&s=<seed, base 36>&z=<rung> when the recipe is the output version's defaults apart from seed and rung (watabou one-line link kept); otherwise &r=<base64url of deflated CBOR recipe delta> (params with preferences folded in, intent, character, entry mode, rerollable salts keyed and schema-checked as Recipe.salts §2.9 VD3-8, table pins and packs differing from shipped - packs by id, version, hash); &l=<base64url of deflated CBOR log> when the town has a log (edits, locks, assignments, style edits, undo and redo; blueprint assignments are log events §7.7); &st=<style id@version> when style not default
values: o, s, z, r, l, st params

statement: A link is emitted only when it can rebuild the same town and picture on any machine: every pack of the document's pack set (base recipe packs plus every pack an adjust in the log names, a selected-then-deselected corpus included; §2.9; VD3-3) is shipped with the link's output version; the base is the recipe (VD4-8: a rebased town is not seed-reproducible); hostContent is empty; the style sheet is shipped; the whole URL fits in 2 000 characters
notes: open item VD5-7 (link for kept town between M2a and M3a)

statement: On a refused link the app states which condition failed (pack not built in; your own name list, also when deselected; host program content; kept from a saved copy; too many edits) and offers the .plat file, or &doc=<ref> when the host configured a DocResolver with publish (§11.5); the document carries pack content and host outputs (§2.9), so the file reproduces the town
preset=<id> never appears in a link: an edited preset elsewhere cannot change the town

Rationale: refuse such links rather than name the pack by id and hash (owner's rule: a shared link never shows a different town); read the pack set, not the base recipe (&l= replays every adjust); refuse for every rebased base (a link cannot name a starting state) (VD4-8)
notes: judgment-call text; cites owner's rule; restated as J-DET-17, J-DET-35, J-DET-50 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Link CI: link to recipe to link identity; model digest built from a link equals the session's; refusal cases - recipe naming a non-shipped pack; district names from a user corpus selected after creation (user:<hash> named only by an adjust; VD2-8, VD3-3); a town that selected then deselected such a corpus, saved and reloaded; a document with a host provider's output; a town rebased by keeping the saved town after a forced load mismatch (VD4-8) - in each the link is refused and the .plat file opened by a library lacking the pack, corpus or provider replays to the session's digest

Retention of old output versions (LC-14): the browser library ships the current output version's model packages plus N-1 and N-2 as lazily loaded, tree-shakable chunks (@plat/*-o<k>; an embed may leave them out); the Node CLI replays any published output version by installing that exact package version; a document or link inside the window replays exactly

Outside the retention window a document opens as a frozen view (§2.9 step 2), checked by chunk content hashes only and labelled 'made with o5; not verified by this version' (its root was computed by o5's packages; VD4-1); a link (no snapshot) opens under the current output version with a visible notice ('made with o5, shown with o8; differences are expected') and the CLI command that replays it exactly; nothing changes silently
The retention window also bounds what the browser can undo by replay (an upgrade, a rebase onto an older version, §7.4): outside it the undo is withdrawn with the CLI command shown

Retention measurement (M3a): each retained output version adds <= 150 KB gzipped to its lazy chunk; golden suite replays under N-1 and N-2; pre-decided fallback: browser window shrinks to N-1 (CLI keeps every version)

Stage-isolated goldens (LC-3; §13.3 builds the tooling from M1): the golden store keeps per seed and stage the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs; a release computes each stage's digest by running the new stage code on those frozen inputs, so only stages whose own code or tables changed can differ; each such stage needs a shift record (stage, cause, seeds and statistics that moved, expected direction)

End-to-end goldens are re-signed only with a cascade record listing every downstream stage whose digest moved and showing from the isolated goldens that each moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated golden also moved needs its own shift record
Topology lives on integer centimetres; predicates are exact (§3.2)
Fields, costs and weights are IEEE doubles; + - x / and Math.sqrt are exact by specification; every other real function goes through dmath (the vetted fdlibm port, D-23)

Determinism lint is an allowlist (GEO-31): in model packages and every adapter or provider whose output reaches the model, the only Math members allowed are abs, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sign, min, max, sqrt, imul, clz32, fround, plus arithmetic operators

The allowlist also covers view code whose output reaches a bit-compared digest (VS2-4): @plat/labels, every ObstacleSource and RoleIndex implementation (§14), functions they call, the S14 builder code writing the display-list columns they read (bbox, geometry ranges and GeomTable, layer, z, symbol extents from the style sheet's sizes; a rotated symbol's extent uses dmath), and §8.10's instance function with everything it calls (stamp, grid and line layouts, per-instance look draws, density edge test) whose positions §13.3 compares byte for byte (NR4-3); CI finds this code as the TypeScript import closure of those implementations, column writers and the instance function, so a joining module is linted without being listed; the rest of @plat/render (paint programs, backends, compositing) stays outside (pixels compared by visual regression, §13.3, §13.4)

** is allowed only with a literal integer exponent 0-4 and the build rewrites it into explicit multiplications; every other power goes through dmath.pow (S1's river-width law w0 x acc^0.4 is dmath.pow(acc, 0.4))

Also forbidden in linted code: Math.random, Date, performance, timers, crypto.getRandomValues, DOM access, locale-dependent string ops (toLocaleString, localeCompare, Intl), Array.prototype.sort without a comparator, and any dependence on object-key or Map iteration order beyond insertion order
A division whose divisor is not a non-zero literal must go through ratio() (§3.2 (8)), enforced by the lint

Vendored dependencies are scanned too: every third-party library a kernel adapter imports is vendored at a pinned version and passes the same allowlist scan at each version change; an audit record (library, version, scan result, each exception with its wrapper) is kept in @plat/kernel; a failing library (e.g. one calling Math.hypot) is patched or wrapped in its adapter before adoption
Every sort uses a total-order comparator with an id tie-break (the OS ObjectMap key-order hazard cannot occur)
Pool workers derive each district on an overlay over one frozen base and return it for a lineage-order merge (§3.3); no result depends on arrival order; no model package reads time (§5.1 principle 5)
One boolean and offset engine per output version on every host (D-14, GEO-9): no host may silently run a different engine; changing the engine is an output-version bump with a declared shift

Host providers (LC-31): a host-supplied table arrives as an editTable, editPreset or setStyle event whose content is copied into the log with provenance 'host' (§7.6); host code registered as a provider (ContentProvider, §14) passes a double-run check at registration (same request run twice in two fresh workers returns identical digests); its results are recorded in the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash) and read from there on replay (§2.9, §11.4); setting packs follow the same rule through the packs block (§2.9; NF-D2)
Determinism CI - cross-host: identical digests on Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, workers on and off
Determinism CI - time dilation: the golden suite under a shim scaling every clock read x 10 and x 0.1 gives byte-identical per-stage digests (GEO-2)

Determinism CI - derived-complete digest: every district's S10, S10b, S11 and S12b and the hinterland unit's (S12b named explicitly, NF-P3) derived for 50 METROPOLIS seeds in three random orders with pool sizes 0-3 give identical digests (laziness contract §4.1; §6.2)

Determinism CI - op-order determinism: every declared batch's result identical under permutation of its ops, and every callback-form stage's identical across two runs, a slot renumbering and pool sizes 0-3 (§3.3; VK-6)
Determinism CI - placement digests: per-stop S13b placement digests of the golden suite identical on the five engines, workers on and off (§13.3, §9.1; N-24)
Determinism CI - headless = UI (O11 f)

Determinism CI - replay = session: replaying base and log equals the session's digest on every B-EDIT sequence (§7.3), including the naming-collision fixture of §7.3 (7) (N-1), undo/redo sequences from several sessions, edits during load verification under both choices of a forced mismatch (§2.9 step 4; NR-8), and edits made before a records mismatch, re-applied (§2.9 step 3; VD4-6)

Determinism CI - truncation identity: a B-EDIT sequence folded with its undone pairs kept and truncated gives the same model digest (§7.4), including a redo followed by a user-created entity (same address in both folds, VD2-3), a setAttr(name) + undo pair and a naming rerollLayer + undo pair each followed by a corpus selection (naming records restored, §2.8; VD4-3), and a corpus selection + undo truncated, saved, reloaded and redone with its pack still in packs (§2.9; VD4-7)
Determinism CI - links and documents without their inputs: §6.4's pack, user-corpus, provider and rebased-town cases (VD4-8)

Determinism CI - checks under the recording version: a keptSnapshot-rebased CITY document upgraded across a test output version whose field driver and digest leaf encoding differ from 'from' opens editable after a reload and replays to the session's digest; a frozen view of a fixture written by a test build labelled o(N-3) opens with no mismatch message, while one with a chunk's bytes altered reports damage and refuses the frozenImport rebase (§2.9 steps 2-3, §7.5; VD4-1)
Determinism CI also includes the double-run check of registered providers and the distinct-key test of §6.1

Second implementations (VK-13): the WebAssembly accelerator (§3.7, J-K8) compiles a hot loop from the same integer algorithm and must reproduce its integer outputs byte for byte; cross-implementation test runs the golden suite with accelerator on and off requiring identical per-stage digests; output-neutral, moves no golden; the TypeScript loop stays in every bundle

The Clipper2-WASM engine, adopted only if M0 (a)'s speed criterion triggers §3.7's fallback, cannot reproduce the arrangement engine's integers; it replaces that engine as the single engine on every host: an output-version bump with a declared golden shift - a shift record for every stage reading a boolean, buffer, inset or band (S1 outline repair, S3 reservations, S8 kerbs, S9 corridors, S10 shared-edge bands step (0) wall and margin bands VK2-16, S11 footprints, S12b greenery faces) and cascade records downstream (§6.4, §13.3); its determinism test is (9)'s cross-host one; version pinned and vendored (4), named in the report (§5.4)
Rationale: byte identity required of the accelerator only, because the fallback engine computes different integers by construction; one engine, one digest per host still holds via the cross-host test
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-28 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Plain-words promise: every user change (pin, bend a street, draw river or island, brush prosperity, rename, assign, draw a house, regenerate a block, edit a table, grow an epoch) is recorded in order as a small event on the permanent address of the thing it changes; town = starting point plus events, applied the same on screen and on reopen; touched things are protected; a change reaching a town-wide dependency is announced before it runs with a list of kept / moved / orphaned edits; otherwise regeneration is local and everything outside stays byte-identical

EditBase { seq (from the document's nextSeq; never reset; survives rebase); author 'user'/'host'/'epoch'/'migration'; session (authoring session, per document and author, reused across reloads - its undo and redo stacks; never read by the fold; VD2-4); group? (one undo step); renames?: Rename[] (case-(4) renames the dry run listed and the user confirmed; VD4-4) }

EditBase.renames is carried on any event whose fold re-draws a name because naming inputs changed: a pack-list adjust, a naming editTable or editPreset, an upgrade, a re-derivation reaching S13a, and the unlock, unassign, undo, redo or revert that ends a name's protection (§2.8; VD4-3); a replay or receiving client computing different renames reports a mismatch, as for fates
Rename = { id: Id; from: string; to: string } (name text before and after as the user saw them)
EditScope = { ids: Id[] } or { ring: PolygonCm; key: PlatKey; level: Level }; resolved to the effective scope at dry run and stored resolved
EditFate = { id; fate 'kept'/'carried'/'orphaned'/'discarded'; to?: Id; reason }

FieldStroke = { path: PointCm[]; radiusCm: Cm; falloff 'linear'/'cosine'; amount (relative delta: field units, or cm for terrain); water? 'locked'/'follow' (terrain only; default 'locked', §7.2, §7.3) }

EditEvent = EditBase and one of 46 kinds: lock, unlock (ids, paths? attribute-level locks COV-FTG-C12), pin, unpin, moveVertex, moveCourseKnot, warp, drawWay, drawWater, drawWall, drawGreen, drawBoundary, drawFootprint, build, moveFootprint, swapUse, fill, setAttr, setAttrMany, paint, paintGround, instance, delete, merge, split, join, revert, regenerate, adjust, setField, assign, unassign, moveLabel, hideLabel, setLayer, editTable, editPreset, setStyle, rerollLayer, convert, closeup, epoch, rebase, upgrade, undo, redo
pin / unpin is only ever an explicit user action, never emitted by viewing
moveVertex { key: PlatKey; at: LatticePoint (position before the move); sig: VertexSig (role signature at the edit, §2.2 rule 5); to: LatticePoint }
moveCourseKnot { water: Id; ordinal (knot's ordinal in WaterBody.controls, §2.3); at: PointCm (before); to: PointCm } - a river's control knot is S1's recorded input, not an arena vertex (VK2-12)
warp { key: PlatKey; fromLevel 0 or 1 (1 by default; 0 also moves water and coast); strokes: WarpStroke[] } - one staged warp session committed on Apply

Draw events: drawWay { points; class: WayClass; widthCm }; drawWater { kind: WaterKind; add: PolygonCm[]; subtract?; line?; widthCm? } (add rings unioned, subtract rings = land brush for islands); drawWall { points; kind: Enceinte['kind']; closed }; drawGreen { polygon; kind: Greenery['kind']; densityPerHa? }; drawBoundary { polygon; district? } (snaps to whole L1 cells); drawFootprint { polygon; cls?; use?; heights?: Partial<Heights> }
build { plot; cls; use?; footprint?; heights? }; moveFootprint { id; deltaCm: VecCm; rotateCdeg? }; swapUse { a; b }; fill { scope: EditScope; arrangement: SitePlan['arrangement']; cls? }

setAttr { id; path; value }; setAttrMany { ids (resolved at dry run); query? (what the user asked, for display); path; value }; paint { target 'roofKind'/'roofColour'/'wallColour'; ids (resolved under the brush); brush: BrushPath; value }
paintGround { region; cover; colour? } is a style region (FTG texture brush), outside the model digest

instance { entity; ordinal?; point?; op 'add'/'move'/'remove'/'restyle'; to?; style?: Partial<InstanceStyle> } (LC-20); for an ordinal-addressed event the dry run fills point with the instance's generated position
delete { id }; merge { ids }; split { id; cut: PointCm[] }; join { ids }

revert { id } = 'reset to generated' (COV-MFCG-L08): one undoable event that applies, in reverse log order, the inverses of every logged event whose target is this entity (its own edits only); ctrl / cmd+click (§14 keymap, MFCG's ctrl-click reset)
regenerate { scope: EditScope; mode 'keep'/'newRandom'; rerolls: Record<Id, number> (absolute, per scope entity, rerolls actually used; LC-5, §5.1 (6)); discardEdits?; fates: EditFate[] }
adjust { param; value; fromStage: StageId; fates: EditFate[] } - Adjust and Re-derive from stage k (LC-4)
setField { field 'prosperity'/'density'/'greenery'/'terrain'; stroke: FieldStroke } - a relative delta; the stroke list is composited once (§7.2)
assign { assignment: Assignment }; unassign { id }
moveLabel { id; placement: Placement }; hideLabel { id; hidden } - LabelEntity.pinned / hidden are model data (§9)
setLayer { layer: Layer; spec: Partial<LayerSpec> }

editTable { table: TableId; ops: RowOp[]; provenance? 'host'; fates? (confirmed fates of §7.6's fallback re-derivation from the table's first reader stage; VD4-4) }; editPreset { preset; ops; provenance?; fates? }; setStyle { ops; provenance? }

rerollLayer { concern: RerollableConcern (generated from the concern registry, §6.1); salt (town-wide: the concern's new salt; 0 with ids); ids? (naming only: re-draw these entities' names; VD2-10); salts?: Record<Id, number> (with ids: per-entity salts actually used, §6.3) } (COV-VG-VN-008)
convert { op: ConversionOp } - defined in §4.11: wallToWay, gateToJunction, outskirtToDistrict, demolish, densify, and decline hooks abandon, decay, ruin, clear, rebuild
closeup { district; strategy: FabricStrategyId; params } - logged before the first edit inside a close-up (LC-18, PART II)
epoch { epoch; inputs: EpochInputs } - an epoch is an event in the log (LC-11, §4.11)

rebase { reason: RebaseReason; stateDigest: Hash128; version (output version whose packages computed stateDigest - the document's output version from this event on; a frozenImport sets it to the library's current version, §2.9 steps 2-3; VD4-1); at (the log head its state materialises: the previous event's seq, or h0 when kept after edits during load verification, §2.9 step 4; any other value refused with E_REBASE_AT, nothing appended; §14; VS4-2) } (LC-13)

upgrade { from; to; mapping: MigrationMap (§7.5); baseDigest? (with a rebased base: base.state's model root computed under 'to', checked by later loads under 'to'; §2.9 step 3, §7.5; VD4-1) } (LC-14); undoable
undo { of: seq of the event undone, or of the first event of its group } and redo { of: seq of the undo it reverses } (NF-D1): applied at the head through the same fold (§7.4)
RowOp = { op 'set'/'insert'/'delete'; rowKey; field?; value?; baseRowHash?: Hash64 } - rows by stable key, never by position (LC-22)
WarpKernel = 'displace'/'liquify'/'relax'/'bloat'/'pinch'/'equalize'/'swirl'/'jitter'; WarpStroke = { kernel; centre: PointCm; radiusCm; innerRadiusCm?; strength; dragCm?: VecCm }

No event stores a VertexId, HalfEdgeId or FaceId (§2.2 rule 5, GEO-5): geometry is addressed by entity address, by lattice point with a role signature (bound by resolveVertexAt, never by distance alone), by a water body's address with a course-knot ordinal (moveCourseKnot, §2.3; bound as §7.4's row states), or by a ring
Undo and redo are events like the rest (§7.4): the log only grows, which lets a host store it (§11.3)
The named actions (G-R4; O16-core) are separate operations with distinct semantics, never one flag

Regenerate (keep settings) re-derives the scope with each entity's recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls (§7.3): faithful, byte-identical when nothing upstream changed; used after a lock or drawn constraint

New random advances the reroll of every scope entity by one, written into the event as an absolute map (replay exact; blocks at different rerolls each move on; LC-5); a scope entity whose content comes out unchanged advances again up to three times, and is otherwise reported (§5.1 (6)); the map records the rerolls used

Adjust re-solves with a changed parameter; locality promised only for parameters the control registry (§7.8) lists as consumed at S10 or later or that carry a spatial scope (a district's density, a block's granularity); a parameter consumed earlier (seed, rung, water setting and side, walls, castle option, gate count, planned/organic, wealth level, the recipe's pack list) is offered as Re-derive from stage k: everything from Sk down re-derives with carry-over (§6.3) after the user confirms the edit-fate report (LC-4)
Same kind, new seed = Enter's successor (new document with seed + 1 and same recipe, §6.1); per district (PART II) it is New random on the district
Surprise me = a new document whose intent is drawn from the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and written into its recipe (§7.7)

Warp is MFCG's staged edit (COV-MFCG-L03, COV-NG-CR02): strokes preview on the L1 overlay at interactive rate (vertex moves and a redraw of affected tiles, no invariants, §8.8); Apply commits one warp event holding the strokes in order (committed only on Apply); Discard drops them

On Apply and every replay each warp stroke is applied as its operation to the geometry current at that log position, never as stored displacements (LC-27): the operation computes a displacement field over the vertices under the brush and the kernel's warp(field, fromLevel, region) applies it

Kernel warp: whole-step validation (swept triangles, every moved edge >= minEdge, one vertex per lattice point, clearance invariant), deterministic halving (at most 8), Steiner re-seating, sliding of vertices on fixed coarser routes, held vertices of locked or pinned entities (listed by the dry run), local re-derivation of any face then failing a class floor, logged (§3.6, GEO-10, GEO-35, VK-7)

Point-standing records (pins, point decorations, positional instance overrides, pinned label placements) move with their host face; every footprint, trace and deck the warp moved is re-based on the ground it now stands on (§7.4 'Warp and what stands on the ground'; VK2-13)
A warp with fromLevel = 0 that moves water hands the moved shores to S1's water operator as its new water (§7.3 (b) 1)

Warp kernels vs MFCG tools: Displace = displace (drags vertices by dragCm, full weight inside innerRadiusCm, falling linearly to 0 at radiusCm); Liquify = liquify (as displace with smooth cosine falloff over the whole radius); Relax = relax (Laplacian relaxation toward equal edge lengths); Bloat = bloat (each L1 cell under the brush grows about its centroid by strength, neighbours yielding); Pinch = pinch (cell shrinks about centroid); Equalize = equalize (each cell moves vertices toward equal interior angles); swirl (own local rotation about brush centre, not MFCG); jitter (seeded random displacement from warp.jitter)

MFCG Rotate maps to the 'rotation' view key (§2.9): whole-map rotation about the frame centre as view state, never a vertex operation (would re-snap every vertex, §3.6); model north (+y) unchanged; the compass is decoupled - view key trueNorth (default: keeps pointing at model north) or free (own angle, MFCG's behaviour)
notes: view keys owned by §2.9; compass by §9.5

statement: MFCG Measure maps to §9.5's measure tool: polyline length in metres and feet, an area mode, snapping to way centrelines, face edges and vertices; view data, no model event (NF-S9)

Rationale: view rotation over rotating model coordinates (wind, sun, aspect, slope read model north; vertex rotation re-snaps the arena); picture exports (SVG, PNG, VTT) use the view's rotation while GeoJSON keeps model coordinates and records the rotation
notes: contains a normative export rule (owned by §11); restated as J-DET-15 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Picture exports (SVG, PNG, VTT) use the view's rotation; GeoJSON keeps model coordinates and records the rotation

Drawing at the authoring boundary (GEO-33): pointer samples resampled along arc length to spacing >= minEdge, simplified with topology-preserving Visvalingam at minEdge, a self-crossing stroke split into simple runs before insertChain (§3.4)

drawWater takes add rings (unioned by the boolean engine) and subtract rings (a land brush), so an island is a subtract ring inside an add ring and overlapping sea shapes union (FTG's method); rivers and canals take a line and a width
drawBoundary selects the L1 cells whose area lies at least 50 % inside the drawn polygon; the district boundary becomes those cells' boundary; the dry run shows the snapped boundary before commit

Rationale: snapping to whole cells over invisible district_bound edges, because every seam edge must be typed street, water, wall, reservation boundary (reserve), field, cliff or frame (II.1) for stage 2's SeamContract (§4.12)
notes: seam typing owned by PART II / §4.12; restated as J-DET-14 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: A drawWay of class bridge across a river face becomes a Bridge whose deck is §4.2 S1 (5)'s perpendicular deck at the point where the drawn line crosses the channel's centreline; the drawn way's ends are routed to the deck by S4's operator (§7.3)

drawFootprint (COV-FTG-M01) places a hand-drawn footprint (concave allowed, simple) on the plot containing it; spanning several plots proposes their JOIN in the dry run; on unplotted land (green, residue, field) creates a plot around it with access to the nearest way, or returns a conflict if none is reachable; the host plot's site plan is re-fitted around it as a fixed slot (buildings no longer fitting listed in the fate report)
build places a building of a class on a plot (site plan picks the footprint when none is given) - §4.11's build(...)

moveFootprint moves or turns a footprint; leaving its plot re-homes it to the plot it lands on with both site plans re-fitted; swapUse exchanges two buildings' uses, occupants and assignments atomically (footprints stay); fill forces an arrangement on the scope's plots and re-runs S11 there

paint (COV-FTG-M04) sets roof kind, roof colour or wall colour on every building whose footprint centroid lies under the brush path (ids resolved at dry run and stored); paintGround records a ground-cover region in the style (pixels only)

The tree brush is a batch of instance events on the entities under the brush (§8.10), one undo step; painting trees where no green entity exists first logs a drawGreen (a wood on open land, a yard_planting in a yard) to host them; instance events also carry close-up presentation edits (PART II II.4)
Field brushes are setField strokes (§7.2); the terrain brush's water mode chooses whether water stays (locked, default) or follows the new ground (follow, §7.3)

People (COV-FTG-C12, C13): a lock with paths fixes chosen attributes of a person (name, age, role ...); New random on a person re-derives it with a new reroll keeping locked paths; relations and schedules are not re-derived by a person reroll (town-wide, §10)
setAttrMany edits many entities at once (job, workplace, schedule, household relocation) from a query resolved to ids at dry run and stored, so replay never re-runs the query; one undo step

Edit targets (owner amendment 5), clause by clause: every generated element is editable; every rule table and preset is editable (§7.6) by users via the preference layer and by us via new table versions; edits are first-class events that persist (log, §2.9), undo (§7.4; undo and redo are log events so they work in shared documents), survive regeneration (§7.2-§7.3) and migrate between versions (§7.5); the generator repairs around them locally (§7.3 operators, F-REDERIVE); the preference and override layer sits above the defaults (§7.6)
The entity registry (§2.8) declares each type's edit kinds with their undo path and lifecycle row; a CI test fails if a generated type has none

Edit-target table (15 rows): terrain - setField(terrain) with water locked/follow, drawWater (hollows, lakes), setAttr on site features; water/coast/rivers - drawWater, moveVertex on shores and coasts, moveCourseKnot, setAttr (bank class), delete; ways/junctions/bridges - drawWay (class bridge for a new crossing), moveVertex, warp, split, merge, delete, setAttr (class, width, surface, name; bridge kind); districts - drawBoundary, merge, split, setAttr (kind, character, name), regenerate, adjust, setAttr(fabric)+regenerate = stage-2 template replacement; blocks/plots - split, join, merge, fill, setAttr (use, owner), regenerate, lock, assign; buildings - drawFootprint, build, moveFootprint, swapUse, paint, setAttr (class, heights, roof), delete, convert (demolish, abandon, decay, ruin, clear, rebuild), assign; walls/gates/towers - drawWall, moveVertex, setAttr, delete, convert (wallToWay, gateToJunction); greenery/trees - drawGreen, tree brush, instance, setAttr, delete; fields - setField (prosperity, density, greenery), setAttr on FieldBands (explicit re-banding); names/labels - setAttr (text), moveLabel, hideLabel, rerollLayer(naming) town-wide or ids; layers/style - setLayer, setStyle, paintGround; people/households - setAttr, setAttrMany, lock with paths, regenerate (person scope), pin; close-ups (stage 2) - every kind above after closeup, instance for presentation; rule tables/presets - editTable, editPreset; history - epoch, convert, rebase, upgrade, undo, redo
View keys (rotation, compass, layer choices) change through the view API and are not logged (§2.9)

Dry-run validation (G-R10): every event is validated before commit on the scratch overlay - the schema, the batch-local and stage-end invariants of its scope (§5.3), the edit-fate report of its effective scope with the case-(4) renames (§7.3 item 4); for a chained operator the whole chain runs on the overlay so the report lists every re-sited bridge, re-routed or cut way and re-based building before commit; for undo or redo, the independence check of §7.4

Dry-run conflicts come back as actions (nearest valid position, blocking lock, fates to confirm, dependent events), never silently resolved; a warp that would break an invariant is halved and reported

An E_KEPT conflict (edit would cross or clear finer content an earlier stage made, or content outside a coarse edit's clear region, §3.3) is offered with one resolution: start the re-derivation at the stage that made that content (for a wall's band parts or a margin band's part, S10's step (0) for the touched run's wall strips or the scope's side of the touched stretch; §4.7, §7.3 item 2)
Bridge commands from a host map one-to-one onto these events and are logged with author 'host' (§11; LC-31)

Protection kinds: a locked entity (or locked attribute paths) is a fixed input - regeneration never changes it and re-derives dependants around it; a pinned entity keeps existence and position, other attributes may re-derive; an edited attribute implicitly pins that attribute and the entity's existence against Regenerate and New random (O9 restored, LC-8) unless the user chooses 'discard edits in scope', only by confirming the fate list (§7.3), recorded in the event; an assigned attribute is held at its assignment within drift bounds (§7.7)
Every finer face under a locked or pinned entity is a fixed input too

Under a warp or smoothing step the kernel holds every route vertex of a locked or pinned entity's geometry and of every finer face under it, closed over the endpoints of coarser edges carrying a held Steiner vertex (§3.6), so 'keeps its position' holds for plots, blocks and buildings (no vertex roles); the dry run lists the held entities (VK2-7)
Precedence when protections meet: lock > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rule tables > defaults (§7.7)

Drawn constraints (G-P8; LC-10, GEO-11) - ways, water, walls, greens, district boundaries, footprints - enter the plat through insertChain as mandatory chains with their roles (§3.6) after §7.1's resampling; locked by default; applied at their log position: inserted into the current state and, for the coarsest faces the chain touches, the class's local operator (§7.3) re-derives the affected scope

Drawn-constraint operator mapping: drawn water via S1's water operator (re-sites crossings on moved reaches and re-routes ways that used them); drawn ways via S4's and S5's (arterials re-route to reuse them); drawn walls via S7's run re-trace; drawn boundaries via S6's regrouping; drawn greens via S12 on covered faces; drawn footprints via S11 on the host plot
Session and replay run the same code at the same log position in the same canonical insertion order, so they produce the same digest (§6.5)

'Rebuild around my drawings' (the surviving form of the old insert-before-stage rule): moves drawn constraints into the recipe as constraints of their stages, regenerates the town, shows the diff as a migration does (§7.5), and commits as a rebase (reason drawnConstraintsRebuilt)
Rationale: one ordered fold over hoisting drawn features before their stage (hoisting regenerates a different town around them on every reload)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-6 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Field brushes (LC-27): a stroke is a relative delta over the driver field (FieldStroke); the field = driver field + stroke list composited in log order and clamped once at the end, so undo removes a stroke and re-composites exactly (a per-stroke clamp is not exact: +0.3 then -0.3 on 0.9 gives 0.7)
A field stroke re-derives every block whose plot samples moved by more than tau = 0.01 of the field's range (§4.5), same tau on replay

Bands come from the town's FieldBands record and move only by an explicit setAttr on it or by an epoch, so a stroke in one quarter never re-bands another; an epoch keeps the stroke list and re-composites it over the epoch's new drivers
The terrain brush (LC-7) edits the heightfield raster under S1's terrain operator (§7.3) with the same stroke list and single clamp (to the declared relief limit, §2.3)

Terrain brush water mode 'locked' (default): the stroke's delta is zero on every cell whose centre lies in a water face or within one cell of a shore or bank edge, and under the footprints, bands and decks of locked or pinned entities (lock > drawn geometry); water bodies, courses and widths do not change; the dry run shows the masked cells
Land cells within two cells of the sea keep §4.2 S1 (2)'s floor of sea level + 10 cm, so a lowering stroke cannot sink the coast

Terrain brush water mode 'follow': the stroke may change bed and bank cells; every reach whose bed cells changed is re-traced by S1's water operator (§7.3), which re-sites its crossings and re-routes the ways that used them

In both terrain modes S1's terrain operator re-bases every building, wing, tower, gate, wall vertex, bridge and pier whose terrain samples changed (§7.3), re-runs drainage locally and re-evaluates the terrain-reading field drivers, so the town stands on the new ground exactly as a reload would compute it
Rationale: 'locked' default because the brush mostly shapes ground and moving a river re-routes roads and bridges, a larger edit the user should choose knowingly
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-24 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Effective scope: regenerate(scope) finds the coarsest faces covering the scope at the scope's level; that set (can be larger than the drawn area) is the effective scope, shown before commit; for a chained edit it is the union of every chained operator's scope

Seam exception (NF-P6): a district-scoped re-derivation's effective scope also includes its bounding ways' chains and Corridor records, the half-corridor strips on both sides, the junction wedges at vertices its batches insert or remove on those spines (on a neighbour's side only II.1 (3)'s neighbour step: one corridor_split edge and the one kerb vertex it lands on, promoted, or adds), the neighbouring cells, plots and footprints whose rings pass through those vertices, and the wing rings of buildings on them (§2.6), all changed only by them (a promoted vertex returns to its level when the lane goes, §2.2 rule 3), and the Seam records it is party to (§4.6, II.4)

Fine levels (L1 cells and below) use tree scoping: every unprotected finer entity under the effective scope is discarded and the refinement stages re-run for those faces - recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls for Regenerate (keep settings), advanced rerolls for New random; sound by over-invalidation; the primary mechanism

The batch's rederivesFrom is the first stage the scope re-runs (§3.3); every finer face an earlier stage made - and for a carve or re-carved reach every finer face outside its clear region - is kept (§3.3)

Shared-edge parts (VK-1, VK2-2): S10's step (0) builds, eagerly and on both sides at once, the L3 parts along every L1 edge two face sets share without corridors - a wall trace's band, setback, glacis, tower and gatehouse parts inside its strips, and the 2 m margin bands along the settlement perimeter and along a reservation boundary two districts share (§4.7); their stage rank is S10, so a re-derivation from S8, S9 or S10 clears the parts inside its scope

A scope holding wall-strip faces, or faces bordering the settlement perimeter or a shared reservation boundary, re-runs step (0) for its own side's parts after its S8 and S9 (first when re-deriving from S10), before its plots: bandUnion restricted to the scope's faces, cross edges ending on the shared edge by attraction onto the vertices the other side's parts placed, and the scope's plot, alley and furlong lines ending on the re-laid band's inner edge; the other side is never written; Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district or the hinterland (S12 row) lays the same parts at the same lattice points, byte-identical to the one-click result when nothing upstream changed

Measurement (M2a, B-EDIT): Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district, a walled district and the hinterland on B-CITY-lite seeds is byte-identical; pre-decided fallback if a one-sided re-run ever differs: cover both sides of every shared stretch the scope borders (other side's parts and fronting blocks re-derive from S10 with the scope, declared in the effective scope)
Rationale: one-sided re-run attracted onto the other side's vertices over re-deriving both sides (the band on each side is a function of the shared edge alone)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-29 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: S13a re-derives label candidates inside the scope and draws names only in §6.3's draw cases (no predecessor, reroll, unedited name whose naming inputs changed; VD3-2): a new entity never renames an existing one and a name with unchanged inputs is never re-drawn

After a scoped re-derivation: S14 emits a DisplayDelta for the changed closure (§8.1); tiles meeting the dirty region are invalidated (§8.8); S13b re-decides only placements whose boxes meet it (§9.2)

Replay mode (load verification, migration, undo beyond scoped records) folds the log through exactly the session's code path: every model stage, S13a's scoped delta included, runs at its event's log position (name uniqueness is resolved scope by scope in log order, §9.6; moveLabel, hideLabel and setAttr(name) address LabelEntity records and names S13a creates mid-log; N-1); only view stages are suppressed - S14 and S13b run once at the end

Coarse stages get a local operator each, with pinned boundaries (LC-7): L1 and L0 are not per-face refinements (S4 routes across the frame, S5 grows a town-wide queue, S6 grows districts across cells, S7 traces an enceinte)

Operator chaining: an operator may chain another (S1's water operator chains S4, S5, S6 and S7); the chain's batches commit in the stated order, each operator draws from the operated entity's lineage under its own stage's concerns, and the whole chain runs in the dry run first (§7.1), so session and replay run the same chain at the same log position

Operator row S1 terrain (terrain brush either mode, site features): operator (a) - masked stroke, local drainage, terrain-reading field drivers, exact re-basing, slope re-sampling; in follow mode (b) for every reach whose bed changed; pinned: all water in locked mode, heightfield outside the stroke, every way's geometry; beyond: in follow mode Re-derive from S1 when a course leaves its drainage basin

Operator row S1 water (drawWater, moved shore or coast vertex, moveCourseKnot, warp from level 0, terrain brush in follow mode): operator (b) in §4.11's order (new water, crossings, routes, wall runs and footprint as data; one L1 batch clearing the footprint's partition content, re-laying kept ways through decks, re-tracing crossed wall runs, cutting lesser ways; one L0 batch inserting water through prepared vertices; both declaring the footprint as clear region; then S5, S6, S7, tree scoping, F-REDERIVE); pinned: reaches and coasts outside the edit, every way, wall and district not named in (b), every finer face outside the footprint less the seam exception; beyond: Re-derive from S1 when the course leaves its drainage basin

Operator row S4 (drawWay of an arterial, moved arterial vertex, moved destination, castle placed or resized, deck re-sited or removed by S1's water operator): re-route only arterials whose corridors meet the edit region or whose destination or deck moved, each between its nearest pinned nodes (junctions of degree >= 3 or destination nodes) on either side, over S3's lattice, every deck a fixed graph edge; pinned: their endpoints, every spine outside the region; beyond: Re-derive from S3 when a destination is added or removed (gate count)

Operator row S5 (drawWay of a secondary, a deleted street, a secondary now crossing water off a deck): regrow only inside the affected L1 cells from proposals whose origins lie there, under S5c's legality (water only on a deck); pinned: the cells' boundary spines; beyond: none
notes: open item NP5-2 (S5b main-road step routing)

statement: Operator row S6 (drawBoundary, district merge or split, outskirtToDistrict, land vacated or covered by a moved channel): regroup and re-type only districts touching the region (grower restricted to their cells), then re-lay the margin bands (VK2-2): along every L1 edge without corridors whose sharing changed (moved perimeter stretch, newly shared reservation boundary), S10 step (0) lays the 2 m band on both sides, and where a merge or conversion ends the sharing it removes both parts; blocks fronting such a stretch on either side (neighbour's or hinterland's included) re-derive from S10 and are in the effective scope shown in the dry run; pinned: every other district and every block fronting no changed stretch
notes: open item VK5-1 (tombstones when regroup moves L1 cells)

statement: Operator row S7 (drawWall, moved trace vertex, wallToWay, gateToJunction, a river whose course crosses an enceinte moved): re-trace only the run between the nearest unaffected towers on each side, with water gates where the course now crosses, re-cut the strips' setback and glacis lines along it, re-derive the strip blocks' S10 step (0); pinned: rest of the trace, its gates and strips; beyond: Re-derive from S7 when enceinte kind or gate count changes

Operator row carve (canal, moat or basin drawn by an edit, §4.11): §4.11's way rule (pinned decks for arterials and sole connections, cuts for the rest) and footprint in declared batch order, channel inserted with the footprint as clear region (§3.3); pinned: every way and finer face outside the carve's footprint = channel + (attractCm + bank setback) united with every L1 cell that buffer meets and every L1 cell its way rule and wall re-trace touch (§4.11; VP2-1, NP3-2), less the seam exception; beyond: if the clear region cannot be kept, §3.3's fallback - a declared town-wide re-derivation with the fate report

Operator rows S8-S11: per cell, block and plot (tree scope, item 2; wall-strip blocks and the scope's side of every shared margin band from S10 step (0)); pinned: the other side of every shared edge. S12: the covered hinterland faces and greenery entities; the hinterland unit re-lays its headland parts along the perimeter by step (0) first; pinned: the districts' side of the perimeter
Terrain operator step 1 Stroke: the stroke list is composited on the heightfield and clamped once (§7.2), with locked mode's mask

Terrain operator step 2 Drainage locally: priority-flood filling and flat resolution (§2.3) on the stroke's bounding box dilated by 8 cells with ring cells' levels fixed as spill heights; the box doubles until no ring cell's filled level changes (worst case the whole hydrology grid, §12.4); filled levels go into the drainage arrays (flowDir, flatRank, flowAccum) only, never stored heights, so a brushed hollow stays a hollow and drains to its spill point; accumulation re-propagated downstream along D8 from the box
A new hollow deeper than the lake threshold is reported ('a hollow: draw water to make it a pond or a lake'), never turned into water

B-EDIT terrain fixtures: drainage arrays after the local re-run equal those of a whole-grid re-run on the same heights; pre-decided fallback: re-run drainage over the whole hydrology grid (frame and margin; S1's own cost approx 16-17 ms at CITY, §2.3, §12.4; VK2-15), output-neutral

Terrain operator step 3 Fields: terrain-reading field drivers (elevation above flood line, low and damp ground, §4.5) re-evaluated on the dilated box; blocks whose plot samples moved beyond tau re-derive as for a field brush (§7.2) - the same result a reload computes from drivers and stroke list (§2.9)

Terrain operator step 4 Re-basing exact: every entity on a changed sample re-based by §2.6's per-entity datum step (the function S11 and S7 call): wing baseCm = max(samples) + plinthCm with foundation skirt; a row footprint whose fall exceeds skirtMaxCm re-split into stepped wings (F-SITEPLAN first rung; footprint face and address unchanged); towers and gates from samples under their footprints; wall base profile (VK2-14): each knot whose sample changed takes the new value and a trace vertex with changed sample and no knot gains one (§2.2 rule 5); bridge deckCm and pier deck height from bank elevations plus the clearance row; a user-edited baseCm is kept (fate kept, listed)
notes: datum rule owned by §2.6; also §5.2 F-REDERIVE test

statement: Rationale: exact re-basing of every entity whose samples changed over a tolerance (microseconds per entity; tolerance would depart from §2.6's datum rule)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-24 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Terrain operator step 5 Slopes: every way whose spine crosses changed cells re-samples slopeP95; a way now steeper than its class's limit is reported with an offer to re-route (a regenerate on that way via S4's or S5's operator), never re-routed silently
Terrain operator step 6 Water: in follow mode, (b) runs for every reach whose bed cells changed

S1's water operator (LC-7, VD2-1, VK3-1) runs in §4.11's carve order - finer structure the new water will meet prepared first, then water inserted, then displaced content grows back - because a coarse insertion into finished fabric may meet finer geometry only at vertices an earlier batch of the same edit placed (§3.3); both geometry batches declare the chain's footprint as clear region (as carve batches (1)-(2) do): the preparation clears the footprint's partition content, structural finer edges inside are kept unless re-laid or cut, the coarse batch clears nothing (§3.3 rule 1)

Water operator step 1 New water as data (nothing committed): moved course knot - course between neighbouring knots recomputed by S1's control-polyline construction (§4.2 S1 (3)), moved knot fixed (an edited knot is implicitly pinned, §7.2), width and depth from accumulation, shores = course buffered by width; carve > carveMaxCm returns F-EDIT with the nearest position along the drag within it (F-RIVER)

Water operator step 1 for a follow terrain stroke: each reach whose bed cells changed is re-traced by descent from the nearest pinned upstream point to the first downstream point where the new course meets the old (or its outfall), F-RIVER's re-trace rungs confined to the reach; knots re-sampled at the control spacing with fresh ordinals, except an edited knot, which the new course must pass within half a control spacing of; a descent that does not is an F-EDIT conflict offering to discard that edit (§7.2)

Water operator step 1 for drawWater: the drawn rings (add unioned, subtract removed; a line buffered by its width), a drawn river's or canal's course being its line; for a moved shore or coast vertex or a warp from level 0: the shore chains as the move leaves them (vertex move, or the stroke's field applied to the reach's L0 shore and coast vertices, the rest of the brush moving land fabric at level 1 by §3.6's warp first), course recomputed as their centreline, knots re-sampled from it; nothing re-traced (user's shore is authoritative, §2.3)

Changed reach = the stretch where the new shores differ from the old; an edited coast stretch has its sea side re-lowered and contours clipped (F-CONTOUR); new shore segments take their bank class and kind by §4.2 S1 (7)

Water operator step 2 crossings as data: siteCrossings (§4.2 S1 (5)) runs on the changed reach (sites perpendicular to the new flow, endpoints on the new banks); each old deck on the reach (built bridge or unused site, §2.7) is matched to its successor site = the new site nearest its old midpoint within the search band (crossing.searchBandM, default 120 m; §6.3's bridge row)

Kept ways = ways the new channel + bank setback meets that are arterials, the only connection of streets beyond them to a gate or the plaza (§4.11's rule), or that crossed the changed reach on a deck; they get new routes from S4's router over S3's lattice between their nearest pinned nodes on either side, new channel + attractCm impassable except across a deck, every site a candidate deck and fixed graph edge, a way's own successor site preferred within the detour bound (<= 1.4 x old length); F-ROUTE's rungs decide, so an extra-bridge deck is sited now before insertion

A deck is built at every site a route uses; the deck at an old deck's successor site takes the old bridge's address, name (§6.3) and assignments when its way uses it; every other new site stays a site (two bank vertices on new shores, no span) inserted by (4) with the shores (§2.7, §4.2 S1 (5); NP3-4); a way whose old deck lay on the changed reach but which the new water no longer meets keeps its geometry and its deck, now over land, becomes an ordinary segment in (9)
The run of every enceinte the new or old course crosses is re-traced as data between its nearest unaffected towers, with a water gate where the new course crosses and none at the old (S7's operator)

Water-operator footprint computed last, before any batch: B = new channel and changed old channel + (attractCm + bank setback); footprint = union (exactly, B inside the cells it meets) of every L1 cell that (i) B meets (vacated land and cells S6 re-assigns); (ii) borders a stretch (3) will cut, prune or replace (a kept way's replaced stretch included) or is crossed by a kept way's new route; (iii) borders the old run of a re-traced wall or a stretch of its setback, glacis or intervallum line (3) removes with it (between the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's end towers) or meets the re-traced run + (half band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side) (NP3-2); same rules as the carve's footprint (§4.11); the fate report lists exactly the protected entities inside it

Water operator step 3 one L1 batch: declares the footprint as KernelTx.clearRegion and clears it by §3.3 rule 1 (every finer partition face whose interior meets it, whole; structural finer edges only as re-laid or cut; VK3-1); inserts each kept way's new route and removes the stretch it replaces (every way stays one connected chain); places on the route at the new bank points the two deck_end vertices of each deck it crosses (under a fresh Bridge, to which §6.3's matching hands the old address when (4) removes the old span), the way's edge between them carrying deck beside way (the L0 batch adds none)

Step 3 walls: replaces each crossed wall run by its re-traced run, the water gate's two bank vertices carrying ('gate_end', gate, 0 / 1) under a fresh Gate (§2.2 rule 7; VK3-2) named in banks by (7); removes the old run with the stretches of its strips' setback, glacis and intervallum lines alongside, each through its StretchRef, ends placed by splitThrough at the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's two end towers (new lines cut in (7))

Step 3 cuts: every other way the new channel + bank setback meets, and every way other than a kept way at a gate that the re-traced run's new strips will meet (NP3-2), by F-REDERIVE's way rung: stretch removed through its StretchRef, each land part kept as a way (old-anchor part keeps the address; the other handed to a new way first by retypeEdges' rekey on its StretchRef, §3.4), a stub shorter than the district's minimum block width removed

Step 3 contact names: splits every other L1 edge the new banks will cross that is no way (a settlement-perimeter or district-boundary stretch, a wall strip's setback or glacis line outside a re-traced run) at its two bank points, each carrying an anchor contact name (§2.2 rule 7: the entity of the edge's first own-level row - on a district boundary the district first in id order, on the settlement perimeter the first in id order of the inner district and the hinterland pseudo-district, on a setback or glacis line its enceinte - at that entity's smallest free ordinal, from 2 on an enceinte; VK3-2), the stretch between removed through its StretchRef; prepares the map's border line at its two bank points without cutting it (§3.3 rule 2)
Every stretch a batch removes is a StretchRef (its two end vertices on its chain), never a whole chain (§2.2 rule 5, §3.4)

What the chain may not move - a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity in the new channel + setback or in a new strip, or a reservation there - returns to the dry run as F-EDIT (lock > drawn geometry), with Re-derive from S3 offered for a reservation

Water operator step 4 one L0 batch: declares the same footprint as clear region and clears nothing (§3.3 rule 1); removes the changed reach's old shore stretches (removeEdges on each StretchRef between the points where new shores leave and rejoin old, §3.4); inserts the new shores through the vertices (3) prepared (deck_end, gate_end, contact-name vertices listed in KernelTx.prepared, promoted to L0, contact names stripped, §3.3, §3.6); each deck's span (way's own edge between promoted bank vertices, carrying deck beside way) lies across the water in S1 (5)'s form so no L0 edge crosses water (§2.2 rule 7); each old deck's Bridge address passes to its successor (§6.3); each unused new site's two deck_end vertices placed on the new shores as S1's L0 batch places a site's (§4.2 S1 (5); NP3-4)

Step 4 demotions: an old shore stretch shared with a quay or riverside wall keeps its way or wall row and is demoted to L1 with its L0-only vertices; a deck left over land keeps no L0 edge: where its deck_end rows are L1 (a deck a carve, outer moat or earlier water edit prepared, an F-ROUTE-sited deck included, VD4-10) its bank vertices take L1 at once; where L0 (placed by S1, S3, S4's or an edit's added deck on standing water, or an edit's new site) they keep L0 with no L0 edge until (9) removes the deck's rows (§2.2 rule 3 demotion; VK3-3, VK4-1), so the L0 view stays land and water only

Step 4: new shores split the finer faces they cross, which keep their owners until (6)-(8) re-own them (§3.3 rule 3); the batch meets no finer edge other than the prepared vertices; tree scoping (8) and F-REDERIVE (9) act only inside the footprint, and item 7 (ii) checks byte identity outside it less the seam exception; old decks' and sites' bank vertices on the changed reach leave with their shores except the deck of a way the new water no longer meets, which (9) turns into an ordinary segment
Water operator step 5 S5: lesser connections re-grow inside the L1 cells whose ways (3) cut, from proposals whose origins lie there, under S5c's legality (water only on a deck)

Water operator step 6 S6: each land face of the footprint that (4) split from a pre-edit L1 cell takes the district (or hinterland, or wall_strip typing) of the pre-edit cell that held the larger part of its area; the merged-cell rule (joins the district holding its larger part) applies only where a boundary stretch was removed on land (a cut way) and no boundary re-separates the parts (NP3-3); vacated land joins the district across its longest boundary unless a wall or arterial separates them (then the next longest; ties by id), or the hinterland; every L1 face whose L0 parent is now water leaves its inherited district face set (§2.2 rule 4) and belongs to the water body's faces; perimeter and district boundaries re-typed on the L1 edges now between their face sets; margin bands follow the S6 row (VK2-2)

Water operator step 7 S7: re-cuts the strips' setback, glacis and intervallum lines along each re-traced run from the feet (3) left, closing them on the new banks; builds furniture: towers at its vertices, the water gate's Gate record at the new crossing with banks naming the two gate_end vertices (3) placed, none at the old; strip blocks' band parts come from S10 step (0) in (8)

Water operator step 8 Tree scoping: S8-S12b re-derive every cell of the footprint (vacated land included) by item 2, shared-edge parts included (strips (3) and (7) changed re-run step (0), which the chain declares for NF-P5, §5.3), succession by anchor for what they reproduce and fresh addresses for new faces (§6.3); height samples the carve changed run (a) 2-4 (local drainage, terrain-reading fields, exact re-basing) on what stands outside the footprint
notes: 'the carve changed' in the water operator's text - see note in conflicts (wording)

statement: Water operator step 9 F-REDERIVE: a deck left over land becomes an ordinary segment of its way (removeEdges on ChainRef('deck', bridge) and its two VertexRef('deck_end', bridge, i); demotion takes bank vertices to the way's level and clears kernel pins, §2.2 rule 3; VK3-3, VK4-1), its Bridge a tombstone; a site left over land removed (deck_end rows via removeEdges on VertexRefs, record a tombstone; §2.7; NP3-4); every re-route, cut, pruned stub, succession and demolition listed in the fate report with its lifecycle event

statement: The deck invariant (§5.3) is evaluated once over the chain's touched faces after (9) and holds there; the kernel's own invariants hold at every batch

Rationale: re-lay kept ways through sited decks and crossed wall runs through water gates before inserting water (a coarse insertion meets finer geometry only where prepared); decks at siteCrossings' sites (bridges stand where a regenerated river's would); the L1 batch declares and clears the whole footprint (VK3-1) because a pond in a block or a widened bank changes no L1 edge there
