statement: Edit fates (LC-8): the dry run lists every protected entity in the effective scope - locked, pinned, edited or assigned; hosting a pin; target of a pinned label placement; housing a pinned or edited person; an edited close-up entity - with its fate: kept (fixed input); carried (to its anchor-matched successor, §6.3, after the class-family check: an override moves with the address only if the successor's class family accepts the attribute, never by id alone); orphaned (no successor: edit stays in the log, listed in the document's orphan table, re-attachable); discarded (only with 'discard edits in scope', recorded as supersede events)
The user sees counts and the list and confirms every fate other than kept; confirmed fates are stored in the event; a replay computing different fates reports a mismatch
notes: open item VD5-1 (after upgrade, stored fates re-reported)

statement: A chained edit's report also lists unprotected consequences (bridges re-sited or removed, ways re-routed, cut or pruned, buildings re-based or demolished) with their lifecycle events

Every edit's report lists the names it re-draws by case (4) (old and new text), confirmed before commit like a fate list and stored beside the fates (EditBase.renames; VD4-4); an action whose dry run lists any returns 'confirm' even when its scope holds no protected entity (§11.2); a replay or receiving client computing different renames reports a mismatch; events ending a name's protection (unlock, unassign, undo, redo, revert removing the holding setAttr, lock or assign) run case (4) in their dry run and list and store the rename the same way (§2.8; VD4-3)

Recorded inputs (LC-12, NF-D3): each plot, block and building persists a derivation record (§2.8) of its last derivation's inputs (field samples, band, context and parameter digests, table slices) and every generated name its naming record (§2.8; VD3-2); Regenerate (keep settings) re-derives those kinds with recorded inputs, reproducing an untouched entity byte-identically even after an epoch or field edit elsewhere; re-deriving with current inputs is Adjust

Kinds without a derivation record (ways, districts, walls) re-derive from their current upstream state, which only an explicit edit or an epoch changes; the provenance rebuilt by their last derivation or the verification replay holds what they read (§2.8); their names keep their naming records

The dependency graph is the audit: Provenance.deps (every entity records what it read) serves (a) as the audit of item 7 and (b) as an Adjust optimisation - invalidating exactly the closure of a changed parameter or table slice - only where the oracle has proven that stage's declarations complete; elsewhere tree scoping applies

Oracle (GEO-11, LC-10, IMP-7; every B-EDIT sequence) (i) replay = session: replaying base and log in log order gives the session's model digest on sequences mixing drawn features with later attribute edits, epochs, rebases, undo and redo; includes the naming-collision fixture (N-1): two scoped regenerations in different districts whose new ways draw the same street name, then moveLabel on the second way's label and setAttr(name) on the first - replay names, LabelEntity records and digest equal the session's; and a corpus selection and a naming-row edit with case-(4) renames stored and recomputed equal (VD4-4)

Oracle (ii) outside the scope byte-identical: every entity outside the effective scope keeps its leaf digest; the oracle computes the seam exception (item 1) from the batches' commit records (changed faces per level, portal roles added or removed) and checks each excepted neighbour cell, plot, footprint and wing ring (a stored composition's rings included, §2.6) equal to its prior ring after removing those vertices (NF-P6, NP3-1, NP4-2)
Oracle (iii) content: content and relation digests outside the scope are unchanged

Oracle (iv) faithfulness: Regenerate (keep settings) checked by byte identity; New random checked per regenerated scope against K = 50 independent from-scratch generations of the same scope (same context, rerolls 32 768 + i, i = 0..K-1): for each of median plot area, frontage width, density and attached share, the rank of the regenerated value among the K (references below it plus a uniform draw from 0..t over the t equal references, from the campaign's own stream; exactly uniform on 0..K for a perfect regenerator)

Faithfulness campaign: n = 800 regenerated scopes per nightly run (400 block, 400 district; §13.2; VS2-9); fails when a chi-squared test on the 10-bin rank histogram (expected counts proportional to ranks per bin) rejects at family-wise p < 0.01, Holm over the four statistics; calibrated (executed: 1.0-1.4 % false campaign failures) with >= 99.5 % detection of too-snug (0.8x, 0.6x), too-loose (1.5x) and biased (+0.25 sd) regeneration at rho = 0.8 (>= 99.3 % at rho = 1; 400 scopes caught only 92-95 %); without the randomised tie-break a tied statistic fails every perfect campaign (bench: fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out, fixall_scope_r2_o9c_power.out, fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.out; IMP-7)

Oracle (v) coarse edits (LC-7, VD2-1, VK3-1): course-knot, drawn-water, moved-shore, level-0 warp and terrain-brush sequences in both water modes end with 0 decks over land, 0 off-deck crossings, 0 wings off §2.6's datum rule, 0 footprints in water, every arterial at its destinations or reported unserved, and every bridge that still has a site within the band keeping its address and name

Oracle (v) cont.: a river move across a street grid commits (no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT) with its decks on the kept ways and cuts on the others, every face outside (b)'s footprint byte-identical; a pond drawn inside a block and a river bank widened into its riverside blocks between two bridges each commit with no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT and every face outside the footprint byte-identical (VK3-1)

Oracle (v) cont.: a river moved across a wall between two towers commits likewise, every indexed role unique per ordinal, the water gate's Gate.banks on its two gate_end vertices, no anchor contact name left, 0 NF-P5 violations (NP3-2, VK3-2, VD3-6); a river moved across the settlement perimeter leaves 0 district faces outside the perimeter (NP3-3); a course-knot move replayed after an upgrade that changed S1's knot count binds its knot by address and ordinal or is reported orphaned, never bound to another body's knot (VK2-12)

Oracle (vi) shared-edge identity (VK2-2): Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district, a walled district and the hinterland is byte-identical to the one-click result; after outskirtToDistrict, drawBoundary and a district merge, every L1 edge two face sets share without corridors carries a margin band on both sides and no other edge carries one (item 3's S6 row)

Replay semantics (LC-10): the log is an ordered fold - each event applies to the state its predecessors produced, through the same code path interactively and on replay; nothing is hoisted; epochs, rebases, upgrades, undo and redo are events like any other

Lifecycle lock/unlock/pin/unpin: created by UI or API on any address, optionally attribute paths; read as entity flags derived from the log; persisted in the log; regenerate: a fixed input, dependants re-derive around it; a lock on a name path keeps the naming record dormant and an unlock that frees it runs §6.3 case (4) in its dry run (rename listed, confirmed, stored; VD4-3); undo: inverse event (undo of a lock that frees a name runs case (4); an unlock that re-drew a name keeps an undo record with the former name and naming record); migrate: address mapped (§7.5); an orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint unless the user drops it

Lifecycle setAttr/setAttrMany/paint: bulk query resolved to ids at dry run; read as entity attributes, flags.edited, editedPaths; log; regenerate: an input override at the stage computing the attribute (name: S13a keeps and never re-draws it while edited, naming record dormant; district kind: S6 reads as fixed; heights and roof: S11); implicitly pinned (§7.2); undo: inverse with old values in the undo record; undoing or reverting a setAttr on a generated name returns it to unedited and runs case (4), the rename listed and confirmed and the replaced text kept in that event's undo record (VD4-3); migrate: attribute names schema-versioned with a rename table; unmappable -> orphan, reported

Lifecycle moveVertex/warp: vertex handle stored as lattice point + role signature / staged warp session with Apply; persisted as the operation (arena key, strokes, fromLevel; moveVertex's at with VertexSig), per-vertex displacements only as a verification record; regenerate: whole-step validation (§3.6) - moved edges >= minEdge and against swept triangles, one vertex per lattice point, clearance, global deterministic halving; vertices on fixed coarser routes slide; locked/pinned entities' vertices held; kernel-pinned vertices move (pins constrain smoothing, simplification and cutting); point-anchored records and stored wing rings move with host faces and everything carried is re-based; a move of water goes to S1's water operator; undo record: moved vertices, re-derived faces, promoted/demoted vertices' and edges' former birth levels and flags, former points of displaced records, former wing rings and stored compositions, former bases; migrate: operation replays at its log position; moveVertex binds by resolveVertexAt - exact point, else signature match within the rebind radius, else orphaned and reported

Lifecycle moveCourseKnot (VK2-12): created by dragging a river's control knot; read as WaterBody.controls (§2.3), the knot path controls/<ordinal> in editedPaths (implicitly pinned); persisted: water body address, knot ordinal, at, to; regenerate: S1's water operator, moved knot kept by every later re-trace; undo record: replaced scope of the whole chain and the knot's former position; migrate: binds after the water body's address is carried (§6.3): (1) the knot with that ordinal if within the rebind radius of at (half the body's control spacing, §4.2 S1 (3)), (2) else the nearest knot of that body within the radius (ties by ordinal), (3) else orphaned and reported; never another body's knot

statement: Lifecycle drawWay/drawWater/drawWall/drawGreen/drawBoundary: drawing tools with resampling, snapping (first-crossing split, attraction) and validation at the authoring boundary; entities with existence = built, author user; log (geometry is the payload); regenerate at its log position through its class's local operator (chained operators included); undo record: replaced scope of the whole chain; migrate: same geometry replays at its log position under the new version

Lifecycle drawFootprint/build/moveFootprint/swapUse/fill: building tools; building and plot entities; log; S11 re-fits the host plot(s) with the footprint as a fixed slot, fill re-runs S11 with the forced arrangement; undo record; migrate: replays; a footprint whose host plot is unmapped re-creates a plot around it

Lifecycle delete/merge/split/join/convert (incl. abandon, decay, ruin, clear, rebuild): context actions; lifecycle events with cause; log; structural ops on the plat (§3.4) with dependants re-derived; convert = retypeEdges plus lifecycle events; decline conversions change existence and the drawing (§2.8); a split or join of a chain carrying a profile (way width, wall base, tunnel invert, shore bank kind or class) goes through retypeEdges' rekey on the part's StretchRef (§3.4), giving each part a cut knot carrying the sampled value and dropping a join knot only where the joined profile is unchanged (§2.2 rule 5), the event writing both records' returned profiles (VK2-8); undo record: members resurrect, tombstones return live, both records' former profiles; migrate: same

Lifecycle regenerate/adjust/re-derive from Sk: named actions on an area, district, block, plot or person; report entry and fate list; log: resolved scope, mode, absolute rerolls used, confirmed fates and renames (VD4-4); regenerate per §7.3 with New random's content check (§5.1 (6)); a pack-list adjust and any re-derivation reaching S13a re-draw unedited names citing a changed slice (case (4)), renames listed for confirmation; undo record: faces, entities (names and naming records included), lifecycle events and tombstones of the effective scope, O(scope) - undo restores former names, never re-draws; migrate: the scope replays, fates recomputed and compared

Lifecycle assign/unassign: assignment dialog / host API; assignment fields, flags.assigned; log, blueprint assignments at positions 0..k; regenerate: claims-first re-derivation of its scope (§7.7); an assigned name keeps the naming record dormant and an unassign that frees it runs case (4); undo record; migrate: addresses and criteria; unmapped members re-solve around mapped ones (§7.7)

Lifecycle setField (brush): prosperity/density/greenery/terrain brush with terrain water mode; read as stroke list and composited field or heightfield; log (strokes); field strokes: blocks whose inputs moved beyond tolerance re-derive (§7.2); terrain strokes: S1 terrain operator (local drainage, re-basing, terrain-reading drivers, follow-mode water operator); undo: stroke leaves the list, field re-composites exactly and the operator re-runs on the stroke's region; migrate: strokes are geometry and replay

Lifecycle editTable/editPreset/setStyle: tables editor, presets and style dialogs; read as the override layer (§7.6); log: row operations by key with the base row's hash, confirmed fates of the fallback and renames (VD4-4); regenerate: entities whose derivation record, naming record or provenance cites a changed slice hash re-derive; a changed naming slice re-draws exactly the unedited names citing it (case (4)), listed for confirmation; a predicate table, or a kind whose recorded slices are unavailable, re-derives from the table's first reader stage with fates (§7.6); undo: inverse row operations, re-derived entities (renamed names with former naming records) restored from the undo record, never re-drawn; migrate: a row that changed or vanished in the new table version -> orphan, reported and kept

Lifecycle instance (and tree brush): tree tools (batch of instance events), instance handles; the entity's instance set with overrides; log; applied by ordinal while the entity's lineage is unchanged since the event (no carry or supersession after its seq) and the ordinal's generated position lies within 0.5 x spacing of the recorded point; otherwise re-matched by position to the nearest unclaimed instance within 0.5 x spacing (a superseded entity's overrides move to its supersededBy successor), else orphaned and reported (§8.10; NF-D11); undo inverse; migrate: ordinals geometry-stable only under the same lineage, else re-match by position
notes: instance matching may be restated in §8.10

statement: Lifecycle rerollLayer: 'reroll names / trees / decoration / compass / emblem' (rerollable concerns of §6.1, generated from the registry; names also on chosen entities, ids, VD2-10); read: effective salt = recipe's initial value set by the log's town-wide rerollLayer events; ids-scoped: per-entity salts in the event; log: absolute salts (with ids, the salts actually used after §6.3's advance); regenerate: naming - S13a re-draws every unedited name (town-wide) or listed entities' unedited names, uniqueness by §9.6; instances, crowns, jitter: display only; compass and emblem: furniture only (§9.5); undo: previous salt, for naming the previous names and naming records from the undo record (VD4-3); migrate: replays

Lifecycle revert (COV-MFCG-L08): ctrl / cmd+click, context action; reads the entity's own logged edits; log (one event); inverses of the entity's own events applied in reverse log order at the revert's position, edits to other entities stay; a name the revert frees runs case (4), rename listed, confirmed, stored; undo: inverse re-applies them; migrate: follows the entity's address; an event whose target no longer maps is reported

Lifecycle moveLabel/hideLabel: label handles; the dry run refuses a placement whose box at its stop meets another pinned label's box at that stop, returning the nearest free position (§9.2; N-28); read as LabelEntity.pinned / hidden, model data in the digest (§6.2); log; honoured by S13b's placement (§9); the LabelEntity exists at the event's log position in session and replay because S13a runs per event (§7.3 item 2); undo inverse; migrate: follows the target address, unmapped -> orphan

Lifecycle setLayer/setStyle/paintGround: UI, style dialog; style state (canonical, outside the model digest); log; no model re-derivation, display list rebuilds; undo inverse; migrate: style schema versioned
notes: setStyle also appears in the editTable row (6383) - see conflict C-4

statement: Lifecycle people (pin, setAttr, lock with paths, regenerate a person; LC-16): an explicit action or edit only, never viewing; the pinned or edited fields, everyone else derived; log; pinned and edited people are fixed inputs re-homed to the household that inherits their household's address (§6.3), else orphans reported (§10.3); undo record; migrate: person-table version recorded per household; person keys map through the household's address; orphans reported

Lifecycle closeup (stage 2; LC-18): logged before the first edit inside a close-up; the close-up's entities, a refinement level of the district; log (strategy, params) and later edits; a pure function of the district's committed state, sub-seed, strategy and params; a base re-derivation of the district re-derives its close-up with carry-over, re-matches presentation instance edits by position and reports orphans; undo record; migrate: replays

Lifecycle epoch (LC-11): grow(doc, inputs) (§4.11) or a circumstance-schedule entry; the derived EpochRecord and lifecycle events with cause; log; the incremental path of §4.11 at its log position; undo record: faces and entities the epoch replaced (O(epoch scope)); migrate: a multi-epoch document upgrades by replaying the whole ordered log with a per-epoch diff, or stays pinned to its output version

Lifecycle rebase (LC-13): created by keeping the saved town on a mismatch, Rebuild around my drawings, or editing a frozen import (keeping the old model at an upgrade needs none: the document stays at its own output version, §7.5); read: the document's base; persisted: base state and event, version naming the output version that computed stateDigest (VD4-1), at naming the log head (h0 when kept after edits during load verification, §2.9 step 4), events before at stay in the log; regenerate: replay starts from the rebased state checked against its root of record for the replay's output version (§2.9 step 3) and folds events after at; the rebase event is a no-op for a client whose base it already is; a replay from the recipe folds an undone rebase and its undo as a no-op pair, every event between them undone (a whole-town event is undoable only as the latest live event)

Bridged rebase (VD3-4): on another client a keptSnapshot rebase whose at lies behind the client's head and whose stateDigest differs from the client's root at at installs the snapshot at at from the doc.load bytes the client kept and re-applies the events after at through the fold (fates recomputed, differences reported, undo records rebuilt; §2.9 step 4); one whose stateDigest equals that root changes nothing; any other rebase behind the head (a hand-built log) is a reported no-op; a load whose log holds a keptSnapshot rebase at model.seq with stateDigest = model.digest takes model as that base without asking

Rebase undo (NF-D4): when the previous base is the recipe (always kept in a rebased base) the undo restores it and replays the kept log; when it is an earlier rebased state, that state is the undo record held in the undo section under its cap; past the cap, or when the replay would need an output version outside the browser's window, the undo is withdrawn with a notice (CLI replays any version, §6.4); a redo re-installs the rebased state kept in the undo section under the same cap (past it the redo is withdrawn with a notice); migrate: the rebased state migrates by the schema chain; an upgrade checks it under from against its root of record, then records its root under to as baseDigest (§7.5; VD4-1); not seed-reproducible

Lifecycle upgrade (LC-14): explicit, after the diff (§7.5); read: the document's output version; log with baseDigest for a rebased base and the packs it saved in its mapping (VD4-1, VD4-9); regenerate per §7.5 (rebased base checked under from and re-rooted under to; every pack to stops shipping copied into packs first; mapping hands names on with addresses and re-draws unedited names whose naming slices the new tables changed, listed in the diff); undo record is upgrade.from (NF-D4): undo replays base and log before the upgrade under that version, exactly the pre-upgrade digest; the pre-upgrade checkpoint makes it instant in session; outside the version window the undo is withdrawn with the CLI command shown

Lifecycle undo/redo (NF-D1): ctrl / cmd+Z, ctrl / cmd+shift+Z, API undo(h) / redo(h), a host's doc.apply; read: live or undone status of each event derived from the log; log (of); after the independence check: undo restores its target's scope from the target's undo record; redo re-applies the target at the head, lifecycle events citing the target's seq and its minted addresses the target's own; an undo or redo whose result frees a name runs case (4), rename listed, confirmed, stored; undo is undone by redo and vice versa (exact inverses); migrate: replays, the target's record rebuilt under the new version by the replay

Lifecycle host provider output (LC-31): a host-registered provider's answer after the double-run check (§6.5); read from the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash); read from hostContent on replay, never re-requested; removed with the event that first requested it; replays without the host

Undo and redo are events (SCL-5, NF-D1): undo never removes an event from a shared log; the host stores the log and it only grows (§11.3); { t: 'undo'; of } and { t: 'redo'; of } are appended at the head and applied through the same fold identically by every client and replay

Sessions (VD2-4): a session is an authoring identity per document and author, not per app start; @plat/api mints one (128-bit random value in base 32, outside model packages) the first time an author edits a document and reuses it on every later open: an unshared document stores it in view state (view.keys['session'], outside every digest, saved with the file, §2.9), so reloads continue the same undo/redo stacks; a file made without one (CLI, link) mints on first edit; a bridged client takes the session the host assigns in doc.load (§11.3; host keeps one per user and document) and never writes the view key; the session enters the log only as EditBase.session; the fold never reads it
Rationale: session per document and author (stored with unshared documents, host-assigned for shared) over per app start, because undo must survive a reload
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-34 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Undo targets: each session has its own stacks; undo targets the session's latest live event (live unless an undo targets it and no later redo re-applies it); a group counts as one step and of names its first event; redo targets the session's latest undo whose target is still undone; a new event from the session clears its redo stack; an unshared document has one stored session so undo there is linear and continues across reloads
A session with the owner role (the app's role for an unshared document) may name any live event (undo(h, of), §11.2), which is how events of an earlier session are undone

Undo record: every committed event keeps the inverse event when one is exact, otherwise the faces, entity records, lifecycle events and tombstones its effective scope replaced, the former birth levels, split flags and stripped contact names of the vertices it promoted, the former levels and flags of vertices and edges it demoted or unflagged (§2.2 rule 3; CommitRecord.promoted, demoted, unflagged), and its touched set (addresses created, changed or removed); undo costs O(scope), never a model copy

undo restores the target's scope from its record and withdraws the addresses the target minted (§6.3); redo re-applies the target at the head from its stored already-resolved payload (scope, absolute rerolls, confirmed fates), reproducing the target's result exactly

Independence check: an undo is applied only if every live event after its target is independent - the later event's touched set and effective-scope faces are disjoint from the target's touched set and the target's effective-scope faces dilated by one ring of adjacent faces at the coarsest level either touches; otherwise the dry run returns an F-EDIT conflict listing dependent events and authors; the session may undo its own dependent events first and an owner may undo through a chain; a redo is checked the same way against live events after its undo

Every client folds the same events in the host's order on the same state, so the check has the same outcome everywhere; an undo or redo whose check fails at its log position (only possible in a hand-built log) is a reported no-op identically on every client and on replay; a whole-town event (upgrade, rebase, Re-derive from S1) is undoable only while it is the latest live event

Undo records are kept for the session and saved in the file's undo section: the last 64 events or 20 MB, whichever is smaller (rebase and upgrade records as their rows state), so undo survives a reload

A client holding no record for a target (joined after it, or record left the cap) rebuilds it by replaying from its nearest checkpoint before the target or from the base, and says it is slow; the replay keeps full records only for events later undo events target (found by a log pre-scan) and touched sets for all; deterministic, so every client reaches the same state

Truncation, in unshared documents only (VD2-3): when an unshared document's undo targets the immediately preceding event, the engine may drop both from the log and hold the target on the session's redo stack; a redo re-appends the target with its original seq and advances nextSeq by one (the seq the kept log's redo would have spent), so every later event and every user-created address is the same in both logs; canonical nextSeq (§2.9) never moves back; lifecycle block, archive and model digest of the truncated log equal those with the pair kept; the truncated target is held in the saved undo section (UndoRecord.redo, §2.9) so a redo after reload re-appends it; a document attached to a host bridge never truncates

A truncation that drops the last logged event naming a non-shipped pack drops that pack from the pack set, but its content stays in packs while that redo entry names it and leaves at the next save only once the entry is cleared by a new session event or leaves the section's cap (§2.9; VD3-3, VD4-7)

B-EDIT truncation property test over random sequences (§6.5 (9)) folds each both ways (including a redo followed by a user-created entity, setAttr(name)+undo and naming rerollLayer+undo pairs each followed by a corpus selection, a corpus selection+undo truncated, saved, reloaded and redone; VD4-3, VD4-7) and requires equal model digests and equal addresses

Checkpoints: copy-on-write (arenas chunked per district, so a checkpoint costs only chunks changed since the previous one), taken whenever accumulated replay cost since the last passes 80 ms at the session's rung and before every epoch, rebase and upgrade, so any replay from a checkpoint stays <= 100 ms; a load taking §6.2 (iii)'s off-path recomputation also takes one at h0

Undo measurement (M2a): undo of a CITY district regeneration <= 30 ms; undo memory <= 25 % of the model's working set after 100 edits; (M3a) the host-and-three-clients convergence test of §11.3 with interleaved undo and redo from every client; pre-decided fallback: saved undo section shrinks to 16 events and checkpoints every 40 ms of replay cost
values: <= 30 ms; <= 25 % after 100 edits; fallback 16 events / 40 ms

statement: Enumeration test: every EditEvent kind (undo and redo included) has an exact inverse or an undo record (O9 d); save -> load -> save is byte-identical over the canonical form (O9 a)

Rationale: undo and redo as logged events with per-session stacks and a conservative independence check over removing the last event (host-stored log only grows; removal survives only as unshared-document truncation)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-16 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Warp and what stands on the ground (VK2-13): four kinds of record hold a world point and move with the ground: Pin.point (host = Pin.host's faces), Decoration.point (the containing L3 face), the current position of a positional instance override (a move's to, an add's point, for a line layout the recorded generated point) held in the entity's override table (§8.10), and a pinned label's Placement anchor and spine (target's faces, or its corridor for a way, §9.1)

After the kernel's commit the edit layer takes every such record whose host face has a moved vertex (commit record's moved list, §3.3) and computes its new point as its mean-value coordinates in the host face's outer ring before the move applied to the ring after it (+ - x / and sqrt only, §6.5), rounded to the lattice

A record whose new point lies outside its host face or nearer its boundary than its clearance (pin's footprint radius, Decoration.keepClearCm, half an instance spacing, a label's box) is re-seated at the nearest lattice point of the host face inset by that clearance, ties by (y, x); if the inset is empty a generated pin or decoration is re-placed by its placement rule (§4.7 S11, §4.9) and a user's record (override, pinned label, user-placed or edited pin) is orphaned and reported

A record of a locked or pinned entity is held like a held vertex: the warp's whole-step validation requires it to stay inside its host face at its clearance and halves the step otherwise (§3.6); the dry run lists it

A building's stored wing rings (and a stored stage-3 composition's wing, court and room rings and tower centres; §2.6; NP4-2) are carried with its footprint face in the same pass (site-plan slots store no polygon, §2.5) by §2.6's wing-carrying rule (NP3-1): each wing's boundary runs re-read from the moved rings vertex for vertex, every other wing vertex follows its mean-value coordinates in the footprint's rings (outer and holes) rounded to the lattice; a rect failing the convex near-rectangle test becomes a quad (§2.6 rule 3); whole-step validation includes §2.6's check via warp's recordCheck, halving the step on failure; composed wings unite to the moved face, rooms inside, tower centres inside or on it
Every entity whose footprint, trace, deck or pier the move carried is re-based by §2.6's datum step (§7.3 (a) 4), a user-edited base kept
The warp undo record keeps every former point, wing ring, stored composition and base; a replay recomputes the same points and rings by replaying the same operation on the same geometry
Stamp and grid instances are world-anchored patterns and are not displaced; the host's new boundary only decides which of them survive (§8.10)

B-EDIT: a warp dragging a square keeps its fountain inside at the same mean-value coordinates; a warp over a yard keeps a user-moved tree in that yard; a pinned pin at the edge of a warped square halves the step; a warp and a moveVertex over a built block leave every building's wings subdividing its moved footprint (§2.6 test); replay reproduces all four
Rationale: carry point records by mean-value coordinates over leaving them at world positions or re-placing by rule; stamps stay world-anchored as fill patterns
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-31 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: MFCG's recorded edit asks (O9 (f), the list behind B6, twelve users): each is a scripted B-EDIT scenario reporting its locality share (entities outside the effective scope byte-identical) and invariant results (§13.2); 'expressible' counts working, measured edits, not event names

MFCG asks table: add a district = drawBoundary (S6 regroups covered cells; S8-S11 where class band changed); delete a district = merge into neighbour (S6 re-types; S8-S11 where band changed); add roads = drawWay (S4 or S5 operator; S8-S11 in split cells); remove roads = delete way (S5 regrows merged cell or S4 re-routes; S8-S11); move/remove labels = moveLabel, hideLabel (LabelEntity.pinned/hidden only; 0 other model changes; S13b re-decides meeting boxes); set district colours = setStyle thematic row keyed by district address (style only, 0 model changes); add/delete vertices = split, merge, moveVertex (L1 edit; S8-S11 in touched cells); place the castle = setAttr(castle, site) (S4 re-routes castle street; S7 re-traces when on the enceinte; cells under old and new reservations re-derive); size castle grounds = setAttr(castle, baileyArea) (reservation resizes, cells under it re-derive, S7 run when on enceinte); farms in chosen areas = setAttrMany land-use faces to arable (S12); draw walls = drawWall (S7 re-trace or new enceinte and strips; F-REDERIVE on plots in new strips); drag points in the sea = moveVertex on coast L0 (S1 water operator, no re-trace, contours clipped, decks re-sited, footprint cleared, kept ways re-laid, others cut; S5, S6; F-REDERIVE)

Draw bridges = drawWay of class bridge across a river face: a Bridge on §4.2 S1 (5)'s perpendicular deck where the drawn line crosses the channel's centreline - the unused site within crossing.snapM (20 m) of that point, which the drawn way builds, or else a new deck whose two deck_end vertices one L0 batch of two shore splits places first, nothing cleared (NP3-4) - then S4's operator lays the drawn way's ends through them with the deck pinned; §5.3's crossing invariant holds
migrate(doc, to) has two parts: the schema chain and the upgrade

Schema chain: a sequence of pure, versioned transforms over the document format, forward only; a document whose schema is newer than the running library opens read-only with a message (view and export; LC-28)
Upgrade (a new output version) is an explicit, undoable upgrade event (LC-14): the base and the whole ordered log (epochs included) replay under the new output version into a new model

A rebased base is checked then re-rooted (VD4-1): before the replay base.state is decoded under from and its model root compared with its root of record for from (§2.9 step 3) - a mismatch refuses the upgrade with a message, the document staying at from - and the replay decodes it under to; the upgrade records the model root of that decoded state as baseDigest, which every later load under to checks

Upgrade mapping: old entities matched to the new by kind, anchor within the kind's hysteresis radius, class family and, for faces and chains, overlap (IoU >= 0.5), through §6.3's matching routine and budget; a matched entity hands its address to its successor (§6.3); edits follow only through §7.3's class-family check; nothing is matched by string equality

Packs the new version stops shipping (VD4-9): before commit, every pack of the pack set that to does not ship and packs does not hold is copied into packs from from's shipped copy (at hand in the browser where from is inside the window and its chunk carries its packs, §6.4, and in the CLI); the mapping names it in packsSaved, so the upgrade event names the pack and its content stays
A pack copy that would pass §2.9's 2 MB cap is an F-EDIT conflict naming the pack and size, nothing committed, offering removal of the pack (an adjust) or keeping the old model
restated_in: §5.2 F-EDIT 5139 (detection list names only a host provider's output passing the cap)
notes: see conflict C-6; open item VD5-2 (removal offer cannot work)

statement: An unmatched edit is a reported orphan, kept in the log and listed in the orphan table, never silently bound to another entity

An orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint (a drawFootprint, drawWay, drawBoundary or drawWater event appended at the upgrade's position) unless the user drops it, so a locked building stays where it was
A diff (entities changed, orphans, statistics deltas, a per-epoch diff for a multi-epoch document) is shown before the upgrade commits

Upgrade undo (NF-D4): the undo record is the from output version, not a stored copy; undo replays the base and log before the upgrade under from (retained N-1 or N-2 chunk in the browser, any published version in the CLI, §6.4), reproducing the pre-upgrade model exactly, digest included (rebased base checked against its root of record for from); the pre-upgrade checkpoint (§7.4) makes it instant in session; when from has left the browser's window (library updated twice since) the undo is withdrawn there with a notice and the CLI command; the diff stays viewable
Document budget 8 MB (§2.9): a METROPOLIS model alone exceeds it
Rationale: upgrade undo replays under the retained version over storing the pre-upgrade model outside the undo cap (a METROPOLIS model exceeds the 8 MB document budget)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-18 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: The user may instead keep the old model: the document stays at its output version while that version is inside the retention window (§6.4); outside it the document opens as a frozen view and its one edit is a rebase (§2.9)
restated_in: §7.4 rebase row 6392 (keeping the old model at an upgrade needs no rebase)

statement: FTG's 'no way to regenerate old towns with new features' and 'cannot be undone' are the weaknesses answered

MigrationMap { orphans: Id[] (targets of logged edits left without a successor, kept in log, listed in orphan table); packsSaved: { id; version; hash: Hash128 }[] (pack-set packs to does not ship whose content this upgrade copied into packs; VD4-9) }; address hand-offs are recomputed by §6.3's matching routine on every replay, never stored; renames are EditBase.renames (§7.1); a replay recomputes the map and reports a difference as for fates (§7.3 item 4)

Rationale: check a rebased base under from and record its root under to (only roots made by the same version compare; the upgrade is the one moment both packages are loaded; VD4-1); copy a stopped pack into the document at the upgrade over keeping every version's packs in the browser (VD4-9)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-44 (pack-copy half: no J-id found) in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Upgrade tests (M3a): golden suite replays under N-1 and N-2; a corpus of edited documents upgraded across one output version keeps 100 % of edited entities or reports each orphan (O9 e); an upgrade undone, in session and after reload, restores the pre-upgrade digest exactly; a METROPOLIS document's saved size does not grow with its upgrades beyond the upgrade events; a keptSnapshot-rebased CITY document upgraded across a test version with different field driver and leaf encoding opens editable after reload, replays to the session's digest, and undo restores the pre-upgrade digest (VD4-1); a document using a pack to stops shipping holds it in packs after the upgrade and reopens with it once from has left the window (VD4-9)

effectiveParams = defaults(pinned table versions) + packs + preset + userGlobal + documentOverrides + log events, each layer a sparse delta with provenance; setting packs recorded in the recipe or in the adjust that adds them by id, version and content hash (§2.9); the UI shows which layer set a value and the report lists auto-resolved values with reasons (O16 a-b)

Preferences are folded in at creation (LC-15): packs, preset, user's global preferences and document overrides are copied into the recipe's params delta ('from your preferences'); a later change to machine preferences never changes an existing document; applying them is the explicit 'apply my current preferences', logged as one adjust per changed parameter with its locality class

Pack content travels with the document (NF-D2, VD3-3): a pack is data (grammars, corpora, ancestries, religions, appearance templates, roster row operations, style hints, §10.4); the content of every pack-set pack not in the shipped set is copied into the document's packs block with id, version, author and content hash, when the document is created (recipe packs) and when an adjust adds one
notes: pack block owned by §2.9; open item VD5-6

statement: Adding or removing a pack in an existing document is an adjust of the recipe's pack list (param 'packs') - a Re-derive from the pack's first reader stage with the fate report (§7.1)
restated_in: §7.1 Adjust 5897 (pack list is an early parameter)

statement: A pack's content stays in packs while the base recipe or any event of the log names it (a removal included), or a truncated event held on a saved redo stack does (§2.9's pack set; VD4-7)
notes: open item VD5-6 (§10.4 states a narrower rule)

statement: When an added or removed pack changes a naming slice (a grammar row, or the corpus a culture or ancestry row field names), S13a re-draws exactly the unedited names whose naming records cite a changed slice (§6.3 case (4); VD3-2), renames listed for confirmation

A user-uploaded corpus is such a pack (VD2-8, VD3-2, VD3-3): selecting it wherever a corpus is chosen (§10.4) is that adjust, entering it in the pack list as user:<content hash> with shipped: false and content in packs (§2.9); its content is the corpus and the keyed RowOp that sets the chosen corpus field of the chosen culture or ancestry row to it instead of the corpus it replaces (§10.4), so the binding travels in the pack's content and hash; exactly the names drawn from that field re-draw (VD4-5); deselecting is a second adjust removing the entry, content kept while the first names it

A replay resolves every pack by hash from the document first (§2.9), never depending on installation; a link is emitted only when every pack of the pack set is shipped, so never for a town whose history selects a user corpus (§6.4)

Tables have keyed rows (LC-22): every rule table - size ladder, stage regimes, way widths, granularity, site plans, class rules and class families, heights, wall spacing, greenery, drivers, naming, style sheets, the dependency graph, S0's feature probabilities, the work-limit coefficients (§5.1 (5)) - is versioned JSON mapping a stable row key to a row whose cells carry { value, unit, provenance: { source, date, note }, calibratable }
Each table's schema declares its readers (stages consulting it) and its slice kinds (row, weights, bracket, thresholds, match; §2.8)

A naming slice of a culture or ancestry row is one field (VD4-5): a SliceRef of kind row with key <rowKey>/<field>, hashed over that field's value and, for a corpus field, the named corpus's content hash (so the hash changes when the corpus changes; VD3-2); a naming draw cites only fields it read; every other slice (of these rows and every other table) stays a whole row, weight vector, bracket, threshold set or match set (§2.8)
Rationale: field slices for culture/ancestry rows over whole-row slices (a row names several corpora; whole-row slices would re-draw every name through the row)
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-48 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: Overrides are row operations, never positional patches: an override records { op, rowKey, field, value, baseRowHash }; when a newer table version changes or removes that row, the override is reported as an orphan - kept, not applied - with old base row, new row and user value side by side

Invalidation by slice (LC-21, NF-D3): a table edit changes the hashes of the slices it touches and exactly the entities whose recorded slices cite a changed slice re-derive (audited by the oracle, §7.3); recorded slices are read from persisted DerivationRecord.slices (plots, blocks, buildings, §2.8), from persisted NamingRecord.slices for every generated name (§2.8; VD3-2; also in a rebased document), and from the provenance rebuilt by the last derivation or the verification replay for every other kind

Invalidation fallback: where no recorded slices exist (a kind without a derivation record in a document rebased from a kept snapshot or frozen import) and for a row inserted into a table read by predicate (a new class row that may match entities that never consulted it, changing the match slice): Re-derive from the table's first reader stage with the fate report, its confirmed fates stored in the editTable or editPreset event (§7.1; VD4-4)

Host tables (LC-31) arrive as editTable, editPreset or setStyle events whose content is copied into the log with provenance host (source, date, version), so a document replays without its host (§11.4)

Users edit through the tables editor and presets dialog (preference layer); we change the system through new table versions - a declared shift whenever output changes (§6.4); the corpus phase replaces values and updates provenance without code changes; the default path with no edits is byte-identical to the shipped defaults (O10 h)
Three input layers above the parameter vector, all persisted in the recipe: intent, character and circumstances, constraints

Intent (outcome targets): form archetype; size as population / area / buildings with a tolerance; water setting and coast side; gate count; wall rings; planned/organic; wealth level and gradient direction; era and region preset; defence level; density

Intent expansion is a pure function held in data: each intent field maps to internal parameters by { param, fn: 'const'/'linear'/'smoothstep'/'table', args } rows (tables interpolate linearly), evaluated in a fixed order

Expansion rows are continuous (GEO-41): no rounding and no comparison inside a continuous control; a discrete outcome is a probability drawn per entity or a discrete control that declares itself (§7.8)

Expansion examples: wealthLevel in [0,1] -> field.characterOffset = lerp(-0.3, +0.3), granularity.joinMaxBonus = 2 x wealthLevel (fractional part = probability a candidate plot takes one more join, from the plot.join stream), greenery.parkPer1000 = lerp(0.1, 0.8); planned in [0,1] -> growth.headingSigma = lerp(20, 5) degrees per 100 m of street, growth.crossroadProb = lerp(0.02, 0.15), avenues.probability = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, planned) per eligible tier-1 way
notes: example values; the rows live in tables consumed by §4 stages

statement: Every internal parameter is documented (unit, range, effect, provenance, consuming stage) and reachable in the advanced panel (O10 a); the registry test proves 100 %

Surprise me (LC-30) draws every intent field from its declared range and weights on the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and writes the drawn intent into the recipe, so the town's link reproduces it

Character and circumstances: a district character vector (wealth, density, age, function mix, planned/organic, greenery, fortification, building scale) supplied automatically per district and overridable; circumstances (era, economy, lordship, government, biome, season, threat, trade, population, terrain events, landscape toggles) as data presets on a timeline that schedules epoch events - an epoch happens only as an epoch event in the log (§7.1, hook 8)

Assignment { id; granularity 'building'/'neighbourhood'/'dispersed'; target? (one building/plot or one district); dispersed? { count; kind: BuildingClass or string; criteria: PlacementCriteria }; name?; function?; shapeClass?: BuildingClass; drift: DriftBounds (+/- area %, +/- floors, allowed layouts and roof kinds, class family); precedence 'overClassRules'; placed?: Id[] (solver placements, persisted with the event) }
notes: Assignment record may also be in §2

statement: PlacementCriteria { districts?; districtKinds?; prosperityBands?; minSpacingM?; nearM?: { to: 'water'/'gate'/'market'/'centre'/Id; maxM }[]; frontageClass?: WayClass[]; avoid?: Id[] }

PlacementSolver.solve(doc, a: Assignment, fixed: Id[] (mapped placements, kept), exclude: Id[] (locked entities), rng: Stream): KernelResult<Id[]> - greedy max-min-distance by score with a bounded swap pass; reports infeasibility with the nearest achievable count

Precedence at S10-S11: lock > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rule tables > defaults (LC-9); a targeted assignment on a locked entity (or locked attribute path) is an F-EDIT conflict returned as an action (unlock, choose another target, or keep the lock); the dispersed solver never places a member on a locked entity
Rationale: lock above assignment because the owner's hook asks for precedence over the generator's class rules, not the user's locks; a host that must override a lock sends an unlock first
notes: judgment-call text; restated as J-DET-11 in the Judgment calls section (scope part)

statement: One path: a blueprint's assignments become assign events at log positions 0..k at document creation; every assign event (blueprint, dialog or host bridge) runs the same claims-first re-derivation for its scope (S10 step 3 on the target's block or on the blocks of a dispersed assignment's chosen plots, §4.7)

Re-solving: when a dispersed member is superseded without a successor only that member is re-placed, every mapped placement fixed (minimum spacing measured from them), nothing still mapped moves; epochs keep placed members; members are added only by an event changing the count or criteria, then placed with existing members fixed

A whole-neighbourhood assignment sets the district's character and class mix while every building stays individually diversified by class rules within drift bounds; drift bounds are inputs to BuildingGenerator.compose; assignments are events (persist, undo, migrate) and take precedence over class rules (O10 e); stable addresses are §6.3's

Forms catalogue (should-have; schema is the must-have hook): a form is a row { id, constraints, growthProgramme, signature } - constraints (site request, wall rings, plaza position, planned flag, gate count band), growth programme (stage regimes and branch tables, §4.4), morphometric signature (radial share of arterials, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share); initial rows: organic, bastide-grid, linear-street (growth anisotropy a = 8 along the main road, §4.4), radial, hill-acropolis, bridge-town, port-quay-parallel, monastic-close, island-city (shore destinations, §4.2 S3), confluence, twin-town, polycentric (two or three nuclei, §4.2 S3); forms compose by growth stage; O10 (g)'s classifier runs on the signature vector
notes: 'should-have' wording vs no-defer rule - canon to check

statement: Control registry: declares for every control its output metric (e.g. density -> buildings per ha; wealthLevel -> median plot area and greenery share; greenery -> private green share), range, consuming stage (earliest stage reading it), locality class (local: consumed at S10 or later or spatially scoped; or re-derive from Sk, fate report first, §7.1; LC-4), continuity class (continuous or discrete with levels), and a documentation anchor linked as context help; the same fields generate @plat/docs' reference pages (COV-FTG-A25)

Monotone and continuous stated statistically (GEO-41): CI sweep runs each continuous control over 21 evenly spaced steps x 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (METROPOLIS nightly): monotone - mean metric moves in the declared direction between adjacent steps, a reversal of at most 2 standard errors allowed; continuous - no adjacent step moves the mean by more than eps = max(3 SE, 3 x the median adjacent change of the mean); per seed - at most 10 % of seeds jump by more than 5 x the median per-seed step at any one step; formula fixed now, SEs and medians measured by the M1 sweep

Effective scope: the coarsest faces covering an edit's scope at its level (possibly larger than the drawn area), union over chained operators, plus the seam exception; shown to the user before commit; EditScope is stored resolved to it
Touched set: the list of addresses an event created, changed or removed, kept in its undo record; used by the independence check and by edits during load recomputation
Live event: an event is live unless an undo targets it and no later redo re-applies it

Eager model: everything the city LOD draws plus the town-level Allocation and FieldBands records; lazily derived content (close-ups, people, stage-3 compositions) is outside it until an edit materialises it

Shift record = (stage, cause, seeds and statistics that moved, expected direction); cascade record = the list of every downstream stage whose digest moved with proof from the isolated goldens that each moved only through its inputs
Render key: the low 64 bits of an entity's entity key (mixing seed key and lineage), used with the instance ordinal for decoration draws (§8.1 item 5; VD2-6)
Pack set: the base recipe's packs plus every pack an adjust event in the log names, a corpus once selected and later deselected included (§2.9; VD3-3)
h0: the log head at which a load's copy-on-write checkpoint of the decoded state is taken; the rebase at-value when the saved town is kept after edits made during load verification
